sentences.zh: 職官誌

translations.literal: Treatise on Official Posts
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on Official Posts

sentences.zh: 夫官非位無以分貴賤，位非品無以定高卑，是以歷代史官，咸有所紀，皆窮源而討本，期與世以作程。

translations.literal: Now, without office there is no rank by which to distinguish noble from base; without rank there is no grade by which to fix high and low. Therefore historians of every age have all recorded something, each tracing the source and examining the root, hoping to set a standard for the world.
translations.idiomatic: Without offices there are no ranks to separate noble from common; without ranks there are no grades to fix precedence high and low. That is why historians of every dynasty have recorded these matters, tracing origins to their roots so that the world might have a lasting standard.

sentences.zh: 迨乎唐祚方隆，玄宗在宥，采累朝之故事，考眾職之遐源，申命才臣，著成《六典》，其勛階之等級，品秩之重輕，則已備載於其中矣。

translations.literal: When the Tang fortune was flourishing and Emperor Xuanzong held the realm, he gathered precedents of successive courts, examined the distant origins of all offices, charged talented ministers, and completed the Six Institutions; the grades of merit ranks and the weight of official ranks were already fully recorded therein.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang was at its height and Emperor Xuanzong reigned, he collected precedents from successive dynasties, traced the remote origins of every office, and commissioned able ministers to compile the Six Institutions, which already set out in full the grades of merit ranks and the relative weight of official ranks.

sentences.zh: 故今之所撰，不敢相沿，祖述五代之命官，以踵百王之垂範，或厘革升降，則謹而誌之，俾後之為天官卿者，得以觀焉。

translations.literal: Therefore what is written here does not dare simply to follow along; it takes as its model the appointment of officials in the Five Dynasties, to continue the lasting standards of the hundred kings. Where there were reforms, promotions, or demotions, they are recorded with care, so that those who later serve as Minister of the Office of Heaven may observe them.
translations.idiomatic: What follows therefore does not merely repeat the Tang record; it traces how the Five Dynasties appointed officials, continuing the models left by earlier kings. Where ranks were revised, raised, or lowered, the changes are recorded carefully so that future Ministers of the Office of Heaven may consult them.

sentences.zh: 梁開平三年三月，詔升尚書令為正一品。

translations.literal: In the third month of Kaiping 3 of Liang, an edict promoted the Director of the Department of State Affairs to the first rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kaiping 3 of Liang, an edict raised the Director of the Department of State Affairs to first rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 按《唐六典》，尚書令正二品，是時以將授趙州王镕此官，故升之。

translations.literal: According to the Tang Six Institutions, the Director of the Department of State Affairs was second rank, upper grade; at this time the office was about to be granted to Wang Rong of Zhao prefecture, so it was raised.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang Six Institutions the Director of the Department of State Affairs had been second rank, upper grade; the rank was raised because the post was about to be conferred on Wang Rong, military governor of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 後唐天成四年八月，詔曰：「朝廷每有將相恩命，準往例，諸道節度使帶平章事、兼侍中、中書令，並列銜於敕牒後，側書『使』字。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Tiancheng 4 of Later Tang, an edict said: "Whenever the court issues a gracious appointment to a general or minister, following former precedent, military governors of the circuits who bear Grand Councilor, concurrent Palace Attendant, or Director of the Secretariat are all listed with their titles after the edict, with the character 'envoy' written to the side."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Tiancheng 4 of Later Tang, an edict declared: "Whenever the court grants a favor to a general or minister, precedent requires that circuit military governors who also hold Grand Councilor, concurrent Palace Attendant, or Director of the Secretariat have their titles listed after the edict text, with the word 'envoy' added at the side."

sentences.zh: 今兩浙節度使錢镠是元帥、尚父，與使相名殊，承前列銜，久未改正。

translations.literal: Now Qian Liu, military governor of the Two Zhes, is Grand Marshal and Imperial Father; his titles differ from those of envoy-ministers, yet he has continued to be listed in the former way, and this has long gone uncorrected.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu of the Two Zhes circuits is Grand Marshal and Imperial Father—titles unlike those of ordinary envoy-ministers—yet he has long been listed under the old formula without correction.

sentences.zh: 湖南節度使馬殷，先兼中書令之時，理宜齒於相位，今守太師、尚書令，是南省官資，不合列署敕尾。

translations.literal: Ma Yin, military governor of Hunan, when he earlier held the concurrent post of Director of the Secretariat, properly ranked with the chief ministers; now he holds Grand Preceptor and Director of the Department of State Affairs, which are offices of the southern departments and should not be listed at the end of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin of Hunan, when he concurrently held Director of the Secretariat, properly ranked with the chief ministers; he now holds Grand Preceptor and Director of the Department of State Affairs—southern-department posts that should not be signed at the end of edicts.

sentences.zh: 今後每署將相敕牒，宜落下錢镠、馬殷官位，仍永為常式。」

translations.literal: Henceforth, whenever general and minister edicts are issued, the offices of Qian Liu and Ma Yin should be omitted, and this shall remain the permanent rule."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, whenever edicts for generals and ministers are issued, the titles of Qian Liu and Ma Yin are to be omitted, and this shall be the standing rule."

sentences.zh: 梁開平二年四月，改左右丞為左右司侍郎，避廟諱也。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Kaiping 2 of Liang, the Left and Right Assistant Directors were renamed Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department, to avoid the taboo of the temple name.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Kaiping 2 of Liang, the Left and Right Assistant Directors were retitled Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department to avoid the imperial temple taboo.

sentences.zh: 至後唐同光元年十月，復舊為左右丞。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of Tongguang 1 of Later Tang, the former titles of Left and Right Assistant Director were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Tongguang 1 of Later Tang, the offices were restored to their former titles of Left and Right Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 後唐長興元年九月，詔曰：「臺轄之司，官資並設，左右貂素來相類，左右揆不至相懸，以此比方，豈宜分別。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of Changxing 1 of Later Tang, an edict said: "In the censorate offices, official qualifications are established for both sides; the left and right palace attendants have always been comparable, and the left and right chief ministers should not be far apart—in such a comparison, how can they be distinguished?"
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Changxing 1 of Later Tang, an edict declared: "In the censorate, ranks are set for both wings; the left and right palace attendants have always been peers, and the left and right chief ministers should not stand far apart—by that analogy, how can they be treated differently?"

sentences.zh: 自此宜升尚書右丞官品，與左丞並為正四品。」

translations.literal: From this time the official rank of the Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs should be raised, so that he and the Left Assistant Director are both fourth rank, upper grade."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs shall be promoted so that he and the Left Assistant Director are both fourth rank, upper grade."

sentences.zh: 右都省

translations.literal: —The Department of State Affairs—
translations.idiomatic: —The Department of State Affairs—

sentences.zh: 後唐長興四年九月，敕：「馮赟有經邦之茂業，宜進位於公臺，但緣平章事字犯其父名，不欲斥其家諱，可改同平章事為同中書門下二品。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of Changxing 4 of Later Tang, an edict said: "Feng Yun has outstanding merit in governing the state and should be advanced to the public terrace; but because the characters for Grand Councilor violate his father's name, and he does not wish to offend his family taboo, Concurrent Grand Councilor may be changed to Concurrent Second Rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Changxing 4 of Later Tang, an edict declared: "Feng Yun's distinguished service to the state merits advancement to the chief ministers' level; because the title Grand Councilor contains characters tabooed by his father's name, and he does not wish to violate his family taboo, Concurrent Grand Councilor is changed to Concurrent Second Rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery."

sentences.zh: 」後至周顯德中，樞密使吳廷祚亦加同中書門下二品，避其諱也。

translations.literal: Later, in the Xiande era of Zhou, the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wu Tingzuo was also given Concurrent Second Rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery, to avoid his taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in the Xiande era of Zhou, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wu Tingzuo received the same title for the same reason of taboo avoidance.

sentences.zh: 晉天福五年二月，敕：「以門下侍郎、中書侍郎並為清望正三品。

translations.literal: In the second month of Tianfu 5 of Jin, an edict said: "The Vice Ministers of the Chancellery and of the Secretariat are both to be prestigious third rank, upper grade."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tianfu 5 of Jin, an edict declared: "The Vice Ministers of the Chancellery and of the Secretariat shall both rank as prestigious third rank, upper grade."

sentences.zh: 」晉天福九月，詔曰：「《六典》云：中書舍人掌侍奉進奏參議表章，凡詔旨制敕、璽書策命，皆按故事起草進畫，既下，則署而行之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of Tianfu of Jin, an edict said: "The Six Institutions states: the Drafting Attendants of the Secretariat manage attendance, memorial submission, deliberation, and drafting of memorials and reports; all edicts, ordinances, imperial letters, and appointments are drafted according to precedent, submitted for approval, and once issued are signed and carried out."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Tianfu of Jin, an edict declared: "The Six Institutions assigns to Drafting Attendants of the Secretariat the duties of attendance, memorial submission, deliberation, and drafting; all edicts, ordinances, sealed letters, and appointments are to be drafted by precedent, submitted for imperial approval, and once issued signed and promulgated."

sentences.zh: 其禁有四：一曰漏泄，二曰稽緩，三曰違失，四曰忘誤，所以重王命也。

translations.literal: There are four prohibitions: first, leakage; second, delay; third, error; fourth, forgetfulness and mistake—by these the royal command is honored.
translations.idiomatic: Four offenses are forbidden: leakage, delay, error, and careless mistake—thus is the sovereign's command held in weight.

sentences.zh: 古昔已來，典實斯在，爰從近代，別創新名。

translations.literal: From antiquity onward the canonical practice has stood; only from recent times have new names been created separately.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity the proper practice has been established; only in recent times were new titles invented apart from it.

sentences.zh: 今運屬興王，事從師古，俾仍舊貫，以耀前規。

translations.literal: Now that the fortune belongs to a rising king, affairs should follow the ancients, so that the old practice may continue and the former standard shine forth.
translations.idiomatic: Now that a new sovereign has risen, affairs should follow the ancients, restoring the old practice to honor the former standard.

sentences.zh: 其翰林學士院公事，宜並歸中書舍人。」

translations.literal: The official business of the Hanlin Academy should all be returned to the Drafting Attendants of the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: The official business of the Hanlin Academy shall all revert to the Drafting Attendants of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 七年五月，中書門下上言：：有司檢尋長興四年八月二十一日敕：準《官品令》，侍中、中書令正三品，按《會要》，大歷二年十一月升為正二品；

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year, the Secretariat and Chancellery submitted: the relevant offices searched the edict of the twenty-first day of the eighth month of Changxing 4: according to the Statutes on Official Ranks, the Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat were third rank, upper grade; according to the Institutional Compendium, in the eleventh month of Dali 2 they were raised to second rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year seven, the Secretariat and Chancellery reported: the relevant offices had located the edict of 21 August, Changxing 4. Under the Statutes on Official Ranks the Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat were third rank, upper grade; the Institutional Compendium records that in the eleventh month of Dali 2 they were raised to second rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 左右常侍從三品，按《會要》，廣德二年五月升為正三品；

translations.literal: the Left and Right Regular Attendants were third rank, lower grade; according to the Institutional Compendium, in the fifth month of Guangde 2 they were raised to third rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: the Left and Right Regular Attendants were third rank, lower grade; the Institutional Compendium records that in the fifth month of Guangde 2 they were raised to third rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 門下中書侍郎正四品，大歷二年十一月升為正三品；

translations.literal: the Vice Ministers of the Chancellery and Secretariat were fourth rank, upper grade; in the eleventh month of Dali 2 they were raised to third rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: the Vice Ministers of the Chancellery and Secretariat were fourth rank, upper grade; in the eleventh month of Dali 2 they were raised to third rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫正五品，按《續會要》，會昌二年十二月升為正四品，以備中書門下四品之闕；

translations.literal: the Remonstrance Grand Master was fifth rank, upper grade; according to the Continued Institutional Compendium, in the twelfth month of Huichang 2 he was raised to fourth rank, upper grade, to fill the vacancy for fourth rank in the Secretariat and Chancellery;
translations.idiomatic: the Remonstrance Grand Master was fifth rank, upper grade; the Continued Institutional Compendium records that in the twelfth month of Huichang 2 the post was raised to fourth rank, upper grade to fill the fourth-rank slot in the Secretariat and Chancellery;

sentences.zh: 御史大夫從三品，會昌二年十二月升為正三品；

translations.literal: the Censor-in-Chief was third rank, lower grade; in the twelfth month of Huichang 2 he was raised to third rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: the Censor-in-Chief was third rank, lower grade; in the twelfth month of Huichang 2 the post was raised to third rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 御史中丞正五品，亦與大夫同時升為正四品。

translations.literal: the Vice Censor-in-Chief was fifth rank, upper grade; at the same time as the Censor-in-Chief he was raised to fourth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: the Vice Censor-in-Chief was fifth rank, upper grade and was raised to fourth rank, upper grade at the same time as the Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 」敕：「宜各準元敕處分，仍添入令文，永為定制。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Each should be handled according to the original edict, and also added into the statute text as a permanent regulation."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered: "Each rank shall follow the original edict, be entered into the statute text, and stand as a permanent rule."

sentences.zh: 」又詔：「門下侍郎，班在常侍之下，俸祿同常侍。」

translations.literal: Another edict said: "The Vice Minister of the Chancellery ranks below the Regular Attendant, but his salary is the same as the Regular Attendant's."
translations.idiomatic: A further edict declared: "The Vice Minister of the Chancellery ranks below the Regular Attendant but receives the same salary."

sentences.zh: 周顯德五年六月，敕：「諫議大夫宜依舊正五品上，仍班位在給事中之下。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Xiande 5 of Zhou, an edict said: "The Remonstrance Grand Master should remain fifth rank, upper grade as before, and still rank below the Drafting Attendant in Court."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Xiande 5 of Zhou, an edict declared: "The Remonstrance Grand Master shall remain fifth rank, upper grade as before and rank below the Drafting Attendant in Court."

sentences.zh: 」按《唐典》，諫議大夫四員，正五品上，皆隸門下省，班在給事中之下。

translations.literal: According to the Tang Code, there were four Remonstrance Grand Masters, fifth rank upper grade, all subordinate to the Chancellery, ranking below the Drafting Attendant in Court.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang Code there were four Remonstrance Grand Masters at fifth rank, upper grade, all under the Chancellery and ranking below the Drafting Attendant in Court.

sentences.zh: 至會昌二年十一月，中書門下奏，升為正四品下，仍分為左右，以備兩省四品之闕，故其班亦升在給事中之上。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Huichang 2, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized to raise the post to fourth rank, lower grade, and divide it into left and right, to fill the fourth-rank vacancies of the two departments; therefore their court rank was also raised above the Drafting Attendant in Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Huichang 2 the Secretariat and Chancellery petitioned to raise the post to fourth rank, lower grade and split it into left and right to fill fourth-rank slots in both departments, which also moved their court precedence above the Drafting Attendant in Court.

sentences.zh: 近朝自諫議大夫拜給事中者，官雖序遷，位則降等，至是以其遷次不倫，故改正焉。

translations.literal: In recent courts, when one was promoted from Remonstrance Grand Master to Drafting Attendant in Court, the office advanced in sequence but the position fell in grade; therefore, because the order of promotion was irregular, it was corrected.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times promotion from Remonstrance Grand Master to Drafting Attendant in Court advanced one's title in sequence but lowered one's court rank; because that order of promotion was illogical, it was now corrected.

sentences.zh: ──右兩省

translations.literal: —The Two Departments—
translations.idiomatic: —The Two Departments—

sentences.zh: 後唐清泰二年十一月，制：「以前同州節度使、檢校太尉、同平章事馮道為守同空。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Qingtai 2 of Later Tang, an appointment said: "The former military governor of Tong prefecture, Acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Grand Councilor Feng Dao is appointed Acting Minister of Works."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Qingtai 2 of Later Tang, an appointment declared: "The former military governor of Tong, Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Grand Councilor Feng Dao is named Acting Minister of Works."

sentences.zh: 」時議者曰：「自隋、唐以來，三公無職事，自非親王不恒置，於宰臣為加官，無單置者。

translations.literal: Commentators of the time said: "Since Sui and Tang, the Three Dukes had no duties; except for imperial princes they were not regularly appointed; for chief ministers they were additional titles, and there was no case of appointing one alone."
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries remarked: "Since Sui and Tang the Three Dukes held no active duties and were not regularly filled except for imperial princes; for chief ministers they were honorific additions, never sole appointments."

sentences.zh: 」道在相位時帶司空，及罷鎮，未命官，議者不練故事，率意行之。

translations.literal: Feng Dao, while in the chief ministership, had borne Minister of Works; when he left his command he received no other appointment. Commentators unversed in precedent carried it out as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao had held Minister of Works while chief minister; when he left his military command he received no other post. Critics unfamiliar with precedent simply improvised.

sentences.zh: 及制出，言議紛然，或云便可綜中書書下事或云須冊拜開府。

translations.literal: When the appointment was issued, discussion was divided: some said he could at once take charge of Secretariat business below, others that he must receive investiture and appointment to an office with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment was issued, opinion was divided: some held he could immediately oversee Secretariat business, others that he required formal investiture and establishment of a staff office.

sentences.zh: 及就列，無故事，乃不就朝堂敘班，臺官兩省官入就列，方入，宰臣退，踵後先退。

translations.literal: When he took his place in court, there was no precedent; he did not enter the hall to take his place in the order of court. Censorate officials and officials of the two departments entered and took their places first; only then did he enter. When the chief ministers withdrew, he followed close behind and left first.
translations.idiomatic: At court there was no precedent for his place in the order of attendance; he did not enter the hall with the regular court formation. Censorate and two-department officials entered first; only then did he enter. When the chief ministers withdrew, he followed immediately and left ahead of them.

sentences.zh: 劉句又以罷相為僕射，出入就列，一與馮道同，議者非之。

translations.literal: Liu Xu likewise, having left the chief ministership to become Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, entered and left court in the same way as Feng Dao; commentators disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu, having left the chief ministership for Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, followed the same court practice as Feng Dao, which critics condemned.

sentences.zh: 及晉天福中，以李纮為司徒，周廣順初，以竇貞固為司徒，蘇禹珪為司空，遂以為例，議者不復有雲。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin, Li Hong was made Minister of Education; at the beginning of Guangshun of Zhou, Dou Zhengu was made Minister of Education and Su Yugui Minister of Works; thereafter it became precedent, and commentators no longer objected.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jin Tianfu era Li Hong was named Minister of Education; at the start of Zhou Guangshun Dou Zhengu became Minister of Education and Su Yugui Minister of Works; thereafter the practice became routine and critics fell silent.

sentences.zh: ──右三公

translations.literal: —The Three Dukes—
translations.idiomatic: —The Three Dukes—

sentences.zh: 後唐天成元年夏六月，以李琪為御史大夫，自後不復除。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer, Tiancheng 1 of Later Tang, Li Qi was made Censor-in-Chief; thereafter the office was never again filled.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer, Tiancheng 1 of Later Tang, Li Qi was appointed Censor-in-Chief; the office was never filled again.

sentences.zh: 其年冬十一月丙子，諸道進奏官上言：「今月四日，中丞上事，臣等禮合至臺，比期不越前規，依舊傳語，忽蒙處分通出，尋則再取指揮，要明審的。

translations.literal: On bingzi of the eleventh month of winter that year, the memorial-presenting officials of the circuits submitted: "On the fourth of this month, when the Vice Censor-in-Chief assumed office, we by ritual should have come to the Censorate. We expected not to exceed former rules and, following custom, to convey messages from outside; suddenly we were ordered to pass through and leave. We then sought further instructions, wanting a clear ruling."
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi in the eleventh winter month that year, the circuit memorial-presenting officers petitioned: "On the fourth of this month, when the Vice Censor-in-Chief took office, we were obliged by ritual to attend at the Censorate. We expected the usual practice of relaying messages from the antechamber, but were suddenly ordered to pass through and leave. We then sought a clear ruling on what is required."

sentences.zh: 又蒙問：大夫相公上事日如何？

translations.literal: We were also asked: how was it on the day the Censor-in-Chief, the chief minister, assumed office?
translations.idiomatic: We were also asked how matters were handled on the day the Censor-in-Chief, who had been chief minister, assumed office.

sentences.zh: 臣等訴云：大夫曾為宰相，進奏官伏事中書，事體之間，實為舊吏。

translations.literal: We replied: the Censor-in-Chief had once been chief minister; memorial-presenting officials served in attendance at the Secretariat—in substance we were his former subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: We answered that the Censor-in-Chief had once been chief minister and that memorial-presenting officers served at the Secretariat—in substance we were his former subordinates.

sentences.zh: 若以別官除授，合雲傳語勞來，又堅令通出。

translations.literal: If he had been appointed to a different office, it would have been proper to relay greetings of courtesy from outside, yet we were still firmly ordered to pass through and leave.
translations.idiomatic: Had he been appointed to a different post, the customary exchange of greetings from the antechamber would have applied, yet we were still ordered to pass through and leave.

sentences.zh: 臣等出身藩府，不會朝儀，拒命則恐有奏聞，遵稟則全隳則例，伏恐此後到臺參賀，儀則不定者。

translations.literal: We come from frontier commands and do not know court ritual; to refuse the order might bring a report upward, yet to obey would wholly destroy precedent. We fear that hereafter when we come to the Censorate to offer congratulations, the ritual will be unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: We come from frontier commands and do not know court ritual; refusal might be reported to the throne, yet obedience would destroy precedent entirely. We fear that future visits to the Censorate to offer congratulations will lack a fixed ritual.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「御史臺是大朝執憲之司，乃四海繩違之地，凡居中外，皆所整齊，藩侯尚展於公參，邸吏豈宜於抗禮。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The Censorate is the great court's office for upholding the law, the place where the four seas are bound to rectitude. All within and without are put in order by it. Even frontier lords still show themselves in public audience—how can lodge clerks presume to resist proper ritual?"
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The Censorate is the great court's law-enforcement office, where the realm is held to account. All within and without are disciplined by it. Even frontier lords still attend in formal audience—how can lodge clerks presume to defy proper ritual?"

sentences.zh: 遽觀論列，可驗侮輕，但以喪亂孔多，紀綱隳紊，霜威掃地，風憲銷聲。

translations.literal: To see them at once argue their case proves their contempt and disrespect; yet because disorders have been many, regulations have collapsed into confusion, the frost of authority has been swept from the ground, and the voice of the censorate has been silenced.
translations.idiomatic: Their immediate protest proves their contempt; yet through endless turmoil regulations have collapsed, imperial authority has been trampled flat, and the censorate's voice has been stilled.

sentences.zh: 今則景運惟新，皇圖重正，稍加提舉，漸止澆訛。

translations.literal: Now the auspicious fortune is renewed and the imperial design set right again; let there be a little lifting up, and the decadent errors will gradually cease.
translations.idiomatic: Now that fortune is renewed and the imperial order restored, a modest revival of discipline will gradually end these corrupt practices.

sentences.zh: 宜令御史臺，凡關舊例，並須舉行，如不稟承，當行朝典。

translations.literal: The Censorate should be ordered: wherever former precedent applies, it must all be carried out; if they do not comply, the court statutes shall be enforced."
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate is ordered to enforce every former precedent; failure to comply will invoke the court statutes."

sentences.zh: 」時盧文紀初拜中丞，領事於御史府，諸道進奏官來賀，文紀曰：「事例如何？

translations.literal: At that time Lu Wenji had just been appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and was conducting affairs at the Censorate. When the circuit memorial-presenting officials came to congratulate, Wenji said: "What is the precedent?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lu Wenji had just become Vice Censor-in-Chief and was conducting business at the Censorate. When circuit memorial-presenting officers came to congratulate, Wenji asked, "What is the precedent?"

sentences.zh: 」臺吏喬德威等言：「朝廷在長安日，進奏官見大夫中丞，如胥吏見長官之禮。

translations.literal: Censorate clerks Qiao Dewei and others said: "When the court was in Chang'an, memorial-presenting officials who saw the Censor-in-Chief or Vice Censor-in-Chief observed the ritual of clerks meeting their superior."
translations.idiomatic: Censorate clerks Qiao Dewei and others replied: "When the court was at Chang'an, memorial-presenting officers who met the Censor-in-Chief or Vice Censor-in-Chief followed the ritual of clerks greeting their superior."

sentences.zh: 及梁氏將革命，本朝微弱，諸藩強據，人主大臣姑息邸吏，時中丞上事，邸吏雖至，皆於客次傳語，竟不相見。

translations.literal: When the Liang were about to seize power, our court was weak, the circuits held power by force, and sovereign and chief ministers indulged the lodge clerks. When a Vice Censor-in-Chief assumed office, though lodge clerks came, they all conveyed messages from the guest quarters and never met face to face.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang were seizing power our court was weak, the circuits held power by force, and sovereign and ministers indulged lodge clerks. When a Vice Censor-in-Chief took office, lodge clerks who came relayed messages from the antechamber and never met him in person.

sentences.zh: 自經兵亂，便以為常。

translations.literal: Since the military disorders, this has been taken as normal.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars this became the accepted norm.

sentences.zh: 」文紀令臺吏諭以舊儀相見，據案端簡，通名贊拜。

translations.literal: Wenji ordered the censorate clerks to instruct them in the old ritual of meeting face to face: seated upright at the desk, they announced names and performed the bow of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji ordered censorate clerks to instruct them in the old ritual of a face-to-face meeting: seated formally at the desk, names were announced and the bow of praise performed.

sentences.zh: 邸吏輩既出，怒不自勝，相率於閣門求見，騰口喧訴。

translations.literal: Once the lodge clerks left, unable to contain their anger, they went in a body to the Gate of the Imperial Secretariat to seek audience and clamored in loud protest.
translations.idiomatic: The lodge clerks left in a fury, went in a body to the Gate of the Imperial Secretariat to seek audience, and raised a loud outcry.

sentences.zh: 明宗謂趙鳳曰：「進奏官比外何官？

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong said to Zhao Feng: "Compared with outside offices, what rank are memorial-presenting officials?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong asked Zhao Feng, "Compared with outside offices, what rank do memorial-presenting officers hold?"

sentences.zh: 」鳳對曰：「府縣發遞祗候之流也。

translations.literal: Feng replied: "They are of the sort who in prefectures and districts handle dispatch and attendance."
translations.idiomatic: Feng answered, "They are the sort who in prefectures and districts handle dispatch and attendance duties."

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「乃吏役耳，安得慢吾法官。

translations.literal: Mingzong said: "They are mere clerical servants—how can they slight my law officers?"
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong said, "They are mere clerks—how dare they slight my law officers?"

sentences.zh: 」乃下此詔。

translations.literal: Thereupon this edict was issued.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon this edict was issued.

sentences.zh: 晉天福五年二月，以御史中丞為清望正四品。

translations.literal: In the second month of Tianfu 5 of Jin, the Vice Censor-in-Chief was made a prestigious fourth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tianfu 5 of Jin, the Vice Censor-in-Chief was ranked as prestigious fourth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 按《唐典》，御史中丞正五品上，今始升之。

translations.literal: According to the Tang Code, the Vice Censor-in-Chief was fifth rank, upper grade; only now was he raised.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang Code the Vice Censor-in-Chief had been fifth rank, upper grade; only now was the rank raised.

sentences.zh: 三年三月壬戌，御史臺奏：「按《六典》，侍御史掌糾舉百僚，推鞫獄訟，居上者判臺，知公廨雜事，次和西推、贓贖、三司受事，次知東推、理匭。

translations.literal: On renxu of the third month of the third year, the Censorate memorialized: "According to the Six Institutions, the Attending Censor supervises the impeachment of the hundred officials and the investigation of lawsuits; the senior one adjudicates the Censorate and manages miscellaneous affairs of the office; the next handles the western investigation, embezzlement and ransom cases, and matters received by the Three Offices; the next manages the eastern investigation and the petition box."
translations.idiomatic: On renxu in the third month of year three the Censorate reported: "The Six Institutions assigns Attending Censors to impeach officials and investigate lawsuits; the senior adjudicates the Censorate and manages office affairs; the next handles the western investigation, embezzlement and ransom cases, and matters received by the Three Offices; the next manages the eastern investigation and the petition box."

sentences.zh: 」敕宜依舊制。

translations.literal: An edict said they should follow the old system.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that the old system be followed.

sentences.zh: 遂以駕部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事劉皞為河南少尹，自是無省郎知雜者。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liu Hao, Vice Director of the Imperial Carriage Office who concurrently served as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs, was made Vice Governor of Henan; from this time no provincial bureau director again held charge of miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hao, Vice Director of the Imperial Carriage Office who concurrently served as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs, was appointed Vice Governor of Henan; thereafter no provincial bureau director again held that concurrent duty.

sentences.zh: 開運二年八月，敕：「御史臺準前朝故事，以郎中、員外郎一人兼侍御史知雜事，近年停罷，獨委年深御史知雜。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Kaiyun 2, an edict said: "The Censorate, following former-court precedent, had one Director or Vice Director concurrently serve as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs; in recent years this was suspended, and only a senior censor was entrusted with miscellaneous affairs."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Kaiyun 2, an edict declared: "By former-court precedent the Censorate had one Director or Vice Director concurrently serve as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs; in recent years this was suspended and only a senior censor held the duty."

sentences.zh: 振舉之間，紀綱未峻，宜遵舊事，庶葉通規。

translations.literal: In the effort to raise standards, regulations have not been strict; the old practice should be followed, so that the general rules may be harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: In raising standards regulations have not been strict enough; the old practice should be restored so that the general rules may be harmonized.

sentences.zh: 宜卻於郎署中選清慎強幹者，兼侍御史知雜事。」

translations.literal: From among the bureau directors one who is pure, cautious, and forceful should again be chosen to concurrently serve as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs."
translations.idiomatic: A pure, cautious, and capable bureau director should again be chosen to concurrently serve as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs."

sentences.zh: ──右御史臺

translations.literal: —The Censorate—
translations.idiomatic: —The Censorate—

sentences.zh: 後唐同光元年十月，崇政院依舊為樞密院，命宰臣郭崇韜兼樞密使，亦置直院一人。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of Tongguang 1 of Later Tang, the Court for Honoring Governance was restored as the Bureau of Military Affairs; the chief minister Guo Chongtao was ordered to serve concurrently as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and one duty officer of the bureau was also appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Tongguang 1 of Later Tang, the Court for Honoring Governance was restored as the Bureau of Military Affairs; chief minister Guo Chongtao was named concurrent Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and one duty officer was also appointed.

sentences.zh: 晉天福四年四月，以樞密副使張從恩為宣徽使，權廢樞密院故也。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Tianfu 4 of Jin, the Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zhang Cong'en was made Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat; this was because the Bureau of Military Affairs had been provisionally abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Tianfu 4 of Jin, Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zhang Cong'en was appointed Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat because the Bureau of Military Affairs had been provisionally abolished.

sentences.zh: 先是，晉祖以宰臣桑維翰兼樞密使，懇求免職，只在中書，遂以宣徽使劉處讓代之，每有奏議，多不稱旨。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Jin founder had the chief minister Sang Weihan serve concurrently as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; he earnestly begged to be relieved and remain only in the Secretariat, so the Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat Liu Churang replaced him; whenever he submitted proposals, they often failed to please.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Jin founder had chief minister Sang Weihan serve concurrently as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Sang earnestly asked to be relieved and remain only in the Secretariat, so Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat Liu Churang replaced him, but his proposals often failed to please the throne.

sentences.zh: 其後處讓丁憂，乃以樞密印付中書門下，故有是厘改也。

translations.literal: Later, when Churang entered mourning, the seal of the Bureau of Military Affairs was handed to the Secretariat and Chancellery; hence this reform.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Churang entered mourning, the Bureau of Military Affairs seal was handed to the Secretariat and Chancellery, which led to this reform.

sentences.zh: 開運元年六月，敕依舊置樞密院，以宰臣桑維翰兼樞密使，從中書門下奏請也。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Kaiyun 1, an edict restored the Bureau of Military Affairs as before and had the chief minister Sang Weihan serve concurrently as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, following a memorial from the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Kaiyun 1, an edict restored the Bureau of Military Affairs and named chief minister Sang Weihan concurrent Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, as requested by the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 周顯德六年六月，命司徒平章事範質、禮部尚書平章事王溥並參知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Xiande 6 of Zhou, Fan Zhi, Minister of Education and Grand Councilor, and Wang Pu, Minister of Rites and Grand Councilor, were both ordered to participate in the affairs of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Xiande 6 of Zhou, Fan Zhi, Minister of Education and Grand Councilor, and Wang Pu, Minister of Rites and Grand Councilor, were both ordered to participate in Bureau of Military Affairs affairs.

sentences.zh: 梁開平元年四月，始置建昌院，以博王友文判院事，以太祖在藩時，四鎮所管兵車賦稅、諸色課利，按舊簿籍而主之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Kaiping 1 of Liang, the Jianchang Court was first established; Prince of Bo Youwen was made administrator of its affairs. Because when the Taizu was still in his commandery, the troops, chariots, taxes, and various levies of the four commands he governed were administered according to old registers, he now presided over them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Kaiping 1 of Liang, the Jianchang Court was first established with Prince of Bo Youwen as administrator. It managed the troops, chariots, taxes, and various levies of the four commands the Taizu had governed in his commandery days, administered according to the old registers.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，中書門下奏請以判建昌院事為建昌宮使，仍以東京太祖潛龍舊宅為宮也。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized that the administrator of the Jianchang Court should be titled Commissioner of the Jianchang Palace, and that the Taizu's former residence in the Eastern Capital from his days before the throne should serve as the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of that year the Secretariat and Chancellery petitioned that the Jianchang Court administrator be titled Commissioner of the Jianchang Palace and that the Taizu's former residence in the Eastern Capital from before his accession serve as the palace.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，以侍中

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, the Palace Attendant
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year two, the Palace Attendant

sentences.zh: （案：原本有闕文，據《五代會要》，以侍中韓建判建昌宮事。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: the original text is defective here; according to the Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties, the Palace Attendant Han Jian was made administrator of the Jianchang Palace.)>〉
translations.idiomatic: (Note: the original text is defective here; according to the Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties, Palace Attendant Han Jian was appointed administrator of the Jianchang Palace.)>〉

sentences.zh: 判建昌宮事。

translations.literal: was made administrator of the Jianchang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: was appointed administrator of the Jianchang Palace.

sentences.zh: 至十月，以尚書兵部侍郎李皎為建昌宮副使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Li Jiao, Vice Minister of War in the Department of State Affairs, was made Vice Commissioner of the Jianchang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Li Jiao, Vice Minister of War in the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Jianchang Palace.

sentences.zh: 三年九月，以門下侍郎平章事薛貽矩兼延資庫使，判建昌宮事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year, Xue Yiju, Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor, was made concurrent Commissioner of the Extended Resources Treasury and administrator of the Jianchang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year three Xue Yiju, Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor, was named concurrent Commissioner of the Extended Resources Treasury and administrator of the Jianchang Palace.

sentences.zh: 至四年十二月，以李振為建昌宮副使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, Li Zhen was made Vice Commissioner of the Jianchang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of year four Li Zhen was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Jianchang Palace.

sentences.zh: 乾化二年五月，以門下侍郎平章事於兢兼延資庫使，判建昌宮事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of Qianhua 2, Yu Jing, Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor, was made concurrent Commissioner of the Extended Resources Treasury and administrator of the Jianchang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Qianhua 2 Yu Jing, Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor, was named concurrent Commissioner of the Extended Resources Treasury and administrator of the Jianchang Palace.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，廢建昌宮，以河南尹魏王張宗奭為國計使，凡天下金谷兵戎舊隸建昌宮者悉主之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year the Jianchang Palace was abolished; Zhang Zongshi, Prince of Wei and Governor of Henan, was made Commissioner of National Accounts, and all revenues, grain, troops, and arms throughout the realm formerly under the Jianchang Palace were placed under his charge.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year the Jianchang Palace was abolished; Zhang Zongshi, Prince of Wei and Governor of Henan, was named Commissioner of National Accounts and given charge of all revenues, grain, troops, and arms formerly under the Jianchang Palace.

sentences.zh: 至後唐同光四年二月，以吏部尚書李琪為國計使。

translations.literal: In the second month of Tongguang 4 of Later Tang, Li Qi, Minister of the Civil Office, was made Commissioner of National Accounts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tongguang 4 of Later Tang Li Qi, Minister of the Civil Office, was appointed Commissioner of National Accounts.

sentences.zh: 自後廢其名額不置。

translations.literal: Thereafter the title was abolished and the office was not re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the title was abolished and never re-established.

sentences.zh: 後唐同光元年十一月，以左監門衛將軍、判內侍省李紹宏兼內勾，凡天下錢谷簿書，悉委裁遣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Tongguang 1 of Later Tang, Li Shaohong, General of the Left Directorate of the Palace Gate Guards and administrator of the Palace Domestic Service, was made concurrent Internal Auditor; all account books of revenues and grain throughout the realm were entrusted to his judgment and disposal.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Tongguang 1 of Later Tang Li Shaohong, General of the Left Directorate of the Palace Gate Guards and administrator of the Palace Domestic Service, was named concurrent Internal Auditor with authority over all revenue and grain account books throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 自是州縣供帳繁費，議者非之。

translations.literal: From this time the provisioning expenses of prefectures and districts grew heavy, and commentators disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: From this time provisioning expenses in prefectures and districts grew burdensome, and critics objected.

sentences.zh: 又內勾之名，人以為不祥之言。

translations.literal: Moreover, the name Internal Auditor was thought by people to be an ill-omened phrase.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, people regarded the title Internal Auditor as an ill-omened phrase.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，敕鹽鐵、度支、戶部三司，凡關錢物，並委租庸使管轄，踵梁之舊制也。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, an edict placed the Salt and Iron Commission, the Revenue Commission, and the Census Commission—all matters concerning money and goods—under the jurisdiction of the Commissioner of Tax and Corvée Labor, following the old system of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year two an edict placed the Salt and Iron, Revenue, and Census Commissions and all monetary affairs under the Commissioner of Tax and Corvée Labor, following the Liang precedent.

sentences.zh: 天成元年四月，詔廢租庸院，依舊為鹽鐵、戶部、度支三司，委宰臣一人專判。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Tiancheng 1, an edict abolished the Tax and Corvée Court and restored the Salt and Iron, Census, and Revenue Commissions as before, entrusting one chief minister to adjudicate them exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Tiancheng 1 an edict abolished the Tax and Corvée Court and restored the Salt and Iron, Census, and Revenue Commissions, entrusting one chief minister with exclusive oversight.

sentences.zh: 長興元年八月，以許州節度張延朗行工部尚書，充三司使，班在宣徽使之下。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Changxing 1, Zhang Yanlang, military governor of Xu prefecture, acting Minister of Works, was made Commissioner of the Three Commissions, ranking below the Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Changxing 1 Zhang Yanlang, military governor of Xu and acting Minister of Works, was appointed Commissioner of the Three Commissions, ranking below the Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三司置使，自延朗始也。

translations.literal: The establishment of a commissioner for the Three Commissions began with Yanlang.
translations.idiomatic: The office of Commissioner of the Three Commissions began with Yanlang.

sentences.zh: 唐朝已來，戶部、度支掌泉貨，鹽鐵時置使名，戶部、度支則尚書省本司郎中、侍郎判其事。

translations.literal: Since the Tang dynasty, the Census and Revenue Commissions managed currency and goods; the Salt and Iron Commission sometimes had a commissioner appointed by name; the Census and Revenue Commissions were adjudicated by the directors and vice ministers of their bureaus in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tang times the Census and Revenue Commissions managed currency and goods; the Salt and Iron Commission sometimes had a named commissioner, while the Census and Revenue Commissions were overseen by their bureau directors and vice ministers in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，楊慎矜、王鉷、楊國忠繼以聚貨之術，媚上受寵，然皆守戶部、度支本官，別帶使額，亦無所改作。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, Yang Shenjin, Wang Hong, and Yang Guozhong in succession used methods of amassing goods to flatter the sovereign and win favor; yet all retained their original posts in the Census and Revenue Commissions, bearing commissioner titles separately, and made no changes to the system.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era Yang Shenjin, Wang Hong, and Yang Guozhong in succession used revenue-amassing methods to win imperial favor, yet all retained their original Census and Revenue posts while bearing separate commissioner titles and changing nothing in the system.

sentences.zh: 下及劉晏、第五琦亦如舊制。

translations.literal: Later Liu Yan and Diwu Qi likewise followed the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Yan and Diwu Qi followed the same old practice.

sentences.zh: 自後亦以宰臣各判一司，不置使額。

translations.literal: Thereafter chief ministers again adjudicated one commission each, and no commissioner title was established.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter chief ministers again oversaw one commission each without establishing a commissioner title.

sentences.zh: 乾符後，天下兵興，隨處置租庸使以主調發，兵罷則停。

translations.literal: After Qianfu, warfare arose throughout the realm; wherever needed a Commissioner of Tax and Corvée Labor was appointed to manage levies and dispatch, and when the troops were disbanded the office ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After Qianfu warfare spread across the realm; Commissioners of Tax and Corvée Labor were appointed wherever needed to manage levies and were disbanded when troops stood down.

sentences.zh: 梁時乃置租庸使，專天下泉貨。

translations.literal: Under Liang a Commissioner of Tax and Corvée Labor was then established to monopolize the realm's currency and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang a Commissioner of Tax and Corvée Labor was established with monopoly over the realm's currency and goods.

sentences.zh: 莊宗中興，秉政者不閑典故，踵梁朝故事，復置租庸使，以魏博故吏孔謙專使務。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong restored the dynasty, those in power were unversed in precedent and followed the Liang story, restoring the Commissioner of Tax and Corvée Labor and entrusting the commissioner's duties to Kong Qian, a former clerk of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong restored the dynasty, those in power, unversed in precedent, followed the Liang example, restored the Commissioner of Tax and Corvée Labor, and entrusted the office to Kong Qian, a former Weibo clerk.

sentences.zh: 斂怨於天下，斫喪王室者，實租庸之弊故也。

translations.literal: The gathering of resentment throughout the realm and the cutting down of the royal house were in truth due to the abuses of the Tax and Corvée commission.
translations.idiomatic: The gathering of resentment throughout the realm and the ruin of the royal house were in truth due to abuses of the Tax and Corvée commission.

sentences.zh: 洎明宗嗣位，思革其弊，未及下車，乃詔削除使名，但命重臣一人判其事，曰判三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong succeeded to the throne, he wished to reform these abuses; before he had even taken his seat, he issued an edict abolishing the commissioner title and ordering one senior minister to adjudicate the affairs, called Adjudicator of the Three Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong succeeded, he wished to reform these abuses; even before taking the throne he abolished the commissioner title and ordered one senior minister to oversee the commissions as Adjudicator of the Three Commissions.

sentences.zh: 至是，延朗自許州入再掌國計，白於樞密使，請置三司名。

translations.literal: At this time Yanlang came in from Xu prefecture to take charge of national accounts again; he informed the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and requested that the title of the Three Commissions be established.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Yanlang came from Xu to take charge of national accounts again, informed the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and requested establishment of the Three Commissions title.

sentences.zh: 宣下中書議其事。

translations.literal: The matter was announced to the Secretariat for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Secretariat for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 宰臣以舊制覆奏，授延朗特進、行工部尚書，充諸道鹽鐵、轉運等使，兼判戶部、度支事，從舊制也。

translations.literal: The chief ministers memorialized in reply according to the old system, appointing Yanlang Special Advancement and acting Minister of Works, Commissioner of Salt and Iron and Transport for the circuits, and concurrent adjudicator of Census and Revenue affairs, following the old system.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers replied according to the old system, appointing Yanlang Special Advancement and acting Minister of Works, Commissioner of Salt and Iron and Transport for the circuits, and concurrent overseer of Census and Revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 明宗不從，竟以三司使為名焉。

translations.literal: Mingzong did not agree, and in the end the title Commissioner of the Three Commissions was used.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong did not agree, and in the end the title Commissioner of the Three Commissions was adopted.

sentences.zh: 同光元年四月，置護鑾書制學士，以尚書倉部員外郎趙鳳為之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Tongguang 1, a Drafter for the Imperial Escort and Documents was established; Zhao Feng, Vice Director of the Granary Bureau in the Department of State Affairs, was appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Tongguang 1 a Drafter for the Imperial Escort and Documents was established, with Zhao Feng, Vice Director of the Granary Bureau, as its first holder.

sentences.zh: 時莊宗初建號，故特立此名，非故事也。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuangzong had just established his reign title, so this name was specially created; it was not precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong had just established his reign title, so this special title was created; it was not precedent.

sentences.zh: 八月，賜翰林學士承旨、戶部尚書盧質論思匡佐功臣，亦非常例也。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Lu Zhi, Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief and Minister of the Census Commission, was granted the title of Meritorious Minister for Deliberation and Support—also an extraordinary case.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Lu Zhi, Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief and Minister of the Census Commission, was granted the title Meritorious Minister for Deliberation and Support—also an extraordinary case.

sentences.zh: 天成三年八月，敕：「掌綸之任，擢才以居，或自初命而升，或自顯秩而授，蓋重厥職，靡系其官，雖事分皆同，而行綴或異，誠由往日未有定規，議官位則上下不恒，論職次則後先未當，宜行顯命，以正近班。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Tiancheng 3, an edict said: "The charge of managing the imperial brush selects talent for appointment; some rise from their first appointment, others are granted from eminent rank. The office is weighty and not tied to official rank. Though the duties are the same, court precedence may differ—truly because in former days there was no fixed rule: when discussing official rank, high and low were not constant; when discussing order of office, first and last were not proper. A clear command should be issued to set right the near court."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Tiancheng 3 an edict declared: "The charge of managing the imperial brush selects talent for appointment—some rise from first appointment, others from eminent rank. The office is weighty and not tied to rank. Though duties are the same, court precedence differed because no fixed rule existed: official rank was inconsistent and order of office improper. A clear command shall set right the near court."

sentences.zh: 今後翰林學士入院，並以先後為定，惟承旨一員，出自朕意，不計官資先後，在學士之上，仍編入《翰林志》。

translations.literal: Henceforth when Hanlin academicians enter the academy, order shall be fixed by seniority of entry; only the one Expositor-in-Chief, by Our will, regardless of official rank or seniority, ranks above the academicians, and this shall be entered in the Record of the Hanlin Academy."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth Hanlin academicians shall rank by order of entry; only the Expositor-in-Chief, by imperial will regardless of rank or seniority, ranks above the academicians, and this shall be entered in the Record of the Hanlin Academy."

sentences.zh: 」其年十一月，敕：「新除翰林學士張昭遠，早踐綸闈，久司史筆，曾居憲府，累陟貳卿，今既擢在禁林，所宜別宣班序，其立位宜次崔棁。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year, an edict said: "The newly appointed Hanlin academician Zhang Zhaoyuan long served in the imperial brush quarters, long managed the historiographer's pen, once served in the censorate, and rose repeatedly to vice minister; now that he is elevated to the forbidden grove, his court order should be specially announced: his standing place should be next after Cui Zhuo."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of that year an edict declared: "The newly appointed Hanlin academician Zhang Zhaoyuan long served in the imperial brush quarters and as historiographer, once served in the censorate, and rose to vice minister; now elevated to the forbidden grove, his court order is specially announced: he shall stand next after Cui Zhuo."

sentences.zh: （《宋史·張昭傳》：晉天福二年，宰相桑維翰薦昭為翰林學士。

translations.literal: (Song History, Biography of Zhang Zhao: In the second year of Tianfu of Jin, Chief Minister Sang Weihan recommended Zhao as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: (Song History, Biography of Zhang Zhao: In Tianfu 2 of Jin, Chief Minister Sang Weihan recommended Zhao as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 內署故事，以先後入為次，不系官序，特詔昭立位次承旨崔棁。

translations.literal: Within the inner office, precedent ranked by order of entry, not by official sequence; a special edict ordered Zhao's standing place next after Expositor-in-Chief Cui Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Within the inner office precedent ranked by order of entry, not official sequence; a special edict placed Zhao next after Expositor-in-Chief Cui Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 據《宋史》則此敕當在晉天福中，薛史系於唐天成三年後，疑原本有脫誤。）〉

translations.idiomatic: According to the Song History this edict belongs in the Jin Tianfu era; Xue's History places it after Tang Tiancheng 3—the original text is suspected of omission or error.)>〉

sentences.zh: 周顯德五年十一月，詔曰：「翰林學士職系禁庭，地居親近，與班行而既異，在朝請以宜殊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Xiande 5 of Zhou, an edict said: "Hanlin academicians serve in the forbidden court and stand in close proximity; they already differ from the regular court ranks, and at court audience their treatment should be appropriately distinct."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Xiande 5 of Zhou an edict declared: "Hanlin academicians serve in the forbidden court at close proximity to the throne; they already differ from regular court ranks and should receive appropriately distinct treatment at audience."

sentences.zh: 起今後當直下直學士，並宜令逐日起居，其當直學士，仍赴晚朝。

translations.literal: From now on, academicians on and off duty should all attend daily audience; those on duty should still attend the evening court."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth all academicians on and off duty shall attend daily audience; those on duty shall still attend the evening court."

sentences.zh: 」舊制，翰林院學士與常參官五日一度起居，時世宗欲令朝夕謁見，訪以時事，故有是詔。

translations.literal: By the old system, Hanlin academicians, like regular court officials, attended audience once every five days. At that time Emperor Shizong wished them to attend morning and evening for consultation on current affairs; hence this edict.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system Hanlin academicians attended audience once every five days like regular officials. Emperor Shizong wished them to attend morning and evening for consultation on current affairs; hence this edict.

sentences.zh: ──右內職

translations.literal: —Inner Court Offices—
translations.idiomatic: —Inner Court Offices—

sentences.zh: 後唐天成三年五月，詔曰：「開府儀同三司，階之極；

translations.literal: In the fifth month of Tiancheng 3 of Later Tang, an edict said: "Grand General with the Ceremonies of a Commandery is the summit of rank;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tiancheng 3 of Later Tang an edict declared: "Grand General with the Ceremonies of a Commandery is the summit of rank;

sentences.zh: 太師，官之極；

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor is the summit of office;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor is the summit of office;

sentences.zh: 封王，爵之極；

translations.literal: enfeoffment as king is the summit of nobility;
translations.idiomatic: enfeoffment as king is the summit of nobility;

sentences.zh: 上柱國，勛之極。

translations.literal: Supreme Pillar of the State is the summit of merit rank.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Pillar of the State is the summit of merit rank.

sentences.zh: 近代已來，文臣官階稍高，便授柱國，歲月未深，便轉上柱國；

translations.literal: In recent times, when civil officials' ranks rose slightly, they were granted Pillar of the State; before many years passed they were transferred to Supreme Pillar of the State;
translations.idiomatic: In recent times civil officials were granted Pillar of the State as soon as their ranks rose slightly, and transferred to Supreme Pillar of the State before many years had passed;

sentences.zh: 武資不計何人，初官便授上柱國。

translations.literal: for military qualifications, regardless of who the person was, at the first appointment they were granted Supreme Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: for military men, regardless of who they were, Supreme Pillar of the State was granted at first appointment.

sentences.zh: 官爵非無次第，階勛備有等差，宜自此時，重修舊制。

translations.literal: Office and nobility are not without order; rank and merit have their gradations—from this time the old system should be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Office and nobility have their proper order and merit ranks their gradations; from this time the old system should be restored.

sentences.zh: 今後凡是加勛，先自武騎尉，經十二轉方授上柱國，永作成規，不令逾越。

translations.literal: Henceforth, whenever merit rank is added, one must begin from Cavalry Captain of Martial Merit and pass through twelve promotions before Supreme Pillar of the State is granted; this shall be a permanent rule, and transgression shall not be allowed."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth all merit promotions shall begin at Cavalry Captain of Martial Merit and pass through twelve promotions before Supreme Pillar of the State is granted; this shall be permanent and no transgression allowed."

sentences.zh: 」雖有是命，竟不革前例。

translations.literal: Though this command was issued, in the end the former practice was not reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Though this command was issued, the former practice was never reformed.

sentences.zh: 右勛格

translations.literal: —Merit Ranks—
translations.idiomatic: —Merit Ranks—

sentences.zh: 後唐清泰二年秋九月庚申，尚書考功上言：「今年五月，翰林學士程遜所上封事內，請自宰相百執事、外鎮節度使、刺史，應系公事官，逐年書考，較其優劣。

translations.literal: On gengshen in the ninth month of autumn, Qingtai 2 of Later Tang, the Directorate of Merit Examination in the Department of State Affairs submitted: "In the sealed memorial submitted in the fifth month of this year by Hanlin academician Cheng Xun, he requested that from the chief ministers and hundred executors to military governors of the outer commands and prefects—all officials concerned with public affairs—annual written examinations be kept and their excellence compared."
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the ninth autumn month of Qingtai 2 of Later Tang, the Directorate of Merit Examination reported: "In the sealed memorial Hanlin academician Cheng Xun submitted in the fifth month of this year, he requested annual written evaluations comparing merit for all officials handling public affairs—from chief ministers and the hundred executors to frontier military governors and prefects."

sentences.zh: 遂檢尋《唐書》、《六典》、《會要》考課，令書考第。

translations.literal: They then searched the Tang History, the Six Institutions, and the Institutional Compendium for examination regulations and ordered that examination grades be written.
translations.idiomatic: They then searched the Tang History, the Six Institutions, and the Institutional Compendium for examination regulations and ordered that grades be recorded.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 時議者曰：「考績之法，唐堯、三代舊制。

translations.literal: Commentators of the time said: "The method of examining achievement is the old system of Tang Yao and the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries remarked: "The method of examining achievement is the old system of Tang Yao and the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 西漢以刺史六條察郡守，五曹尚書綜庶績，法尤精察，吏有檢繩。

translations.literal: The Western Han used the six articles of the inspectors to examine prefects and governors; the five bureau ministers of the Department of State Affairs summarized all achievements—the law was especially precise, and officials had standards of restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Han used the inspectors' six articles to examine prefects and governors, and the five bureau ministers summarized all achievements—the law was especially precise and officials held to standards of restraint.

sentences.zh: 漢末亂離，舊章弛廢。

translations.literal: At the end of Han came disorder and separation, and the old regulations lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han came disorder and separation, and the old regulations lapsed.

sentences.zh: 魏武於軍中權制品第，議吏清濁，用人按吏，頓爽前規。

translations.literal: Wei Wu in the army provisionally established grades, debated the purity and impurity of officials, and employed men according to clerical rank—suddenly departing from the former rules.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wu provisionally established grades in the army, debated officials' purity and impurity, and employed men by clerical rank—suddenly departing from former rules.

sentences.zh: 隋、唐已來，始著於令。

translations.literal: Since Sui and Tang it was first written into statute.
translations.idiomatic: Since Sui and Tang it was first written into statute.

sentences.zh: 漢代郡守，入為三公，魏、晉之後，政在中書，左右僕射知政事，午前視禁中，午後視省中，三臺百職，無不統攝。

translations.literal: In Han, prefects and governors entered office as the Three Dukes; after Wei and Jin, government lay in the Secretariat, the Left and Right Vice Directors managed affairs, viewing the forbidden palace in the morning and the departments in the afternoon—the three offices and hundred duties were all under their supervision.
translations.idiomatic: In Han prefects and governors rose to the Three Dukes; after Wei and Jin government lay in the Secretariat, the Left and Right Vice Directors managed affairs, viewing the forbidden palace in the morning and the departments in the afternoon—all three offices and hundred duties under their supervision.

sentences.zh: 以是論之，宰輔憑何較考？

translations.literal: Judging by this, by what means can the chief ministers be examined?
translations.idiomatic: By this reasoning, by what means can chief ministers be examined?

sentences.zh: 自天寶末，權置使務已後，庶事因循，尚書諸司，漸致有名無實，廢墜已久，未知憑何督責。

translations.literal: From the end of Tianbao, after commissioners were provisionally established for special duties, all affairs followed inertia; the bureaus of the Department of State Affairs gradually became names without reality, long fallen into disuse—by what means supervision and accountability are to be applied is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: From the end of Tianbao, after special commissioners were provisionally established, affairs followed inertia; Department of State Affairs bureaus gradually became names without reality and long fell into disuse—by what means supervision is to be applied is unknown.

sentences.zh: 」程遜所上，亦未詳本源，其時所司雖有舉明，大都諸官亦無考較之事。

translations.literal: What Cheng Xun submitted also did not clarify the origins; though the relevant offices at the time made some exposition, for the most part the various officials had no examinations or comparisons.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xun's proposal also failed to clarify origins; though relevant offices made some exposition, for the most part officials underwent no examination or comparison.

sentences.zh: 右較考

translations.literal: —Examinations and Comparisons—
translations.idiomatic: —Examinations and Comparisons—

sentences.zh: 周顯德五年十二月，詔：「兩京五府少尹、司錄參軍，先各置兩員，起今後只置一員，六曹判司內只置戶曹、法曹各一員，其餘及諸州支使、兩蕃判官並省。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of Xiande 5 of Zhou, an edict said: "For the vice governors and record-keeping aides of the two capitals and five prefectures, two posts were formerly established for each; from now on only one shall be established. Within the six bureau adjudicators only one Census Bureau and one Law Bureau adjudicator shall be established each; the rest, as well as dispatch officers of the various prefectures and judges of the two frontier commands, are all to be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Xiande 5 of Zhou an edict declared: "Vice governors and record-keeping aides of the two capitals and five prefectures shall be reduced from two posts each to one; among the six bureau adjudicators only one Census Bureau and one Law Bureau adjudicator shall remain; all others, as well as dispatch officers of the prefectures and judges of the two frontier commands, are abolished."

sentences.zh: 右增減

translations.literal: —Additions and Reductions—
translations.idiomatic: —Additions and Reductions—

sentences.zh: 梁開平元年五月，改禦食使為司膳使，小馬坊使為天驥使，文思院使為乾文院使，同和院使為儀鸞院使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of Kaiping 1 of Liang, the Commissioner of Imperial Food was renamed Commissioner of Palace Provisions; the Commissioner of the Small Horse Pasture was renamed Commissioner of Heavenly Steeds; the Commissioner of the Literary Reflection Court was renamed Commissioner of the Dry Literary Court; the Commissioner of the Harmonious Unity Court was renamed Commissioner of the Ceremonial Phoenix Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kaiping 1 of Liang the Commissioner of Imperial Food became Commissioner of Palace Provisions; the Small Horse Pasture commissioner became Commissioner of Heavenly Steeds; the Literary Reflection Court commissioner became Commissioner of the Dry Literary Court; the Harmonious Unity Court commissioner became Commissioner of the Ceremonial Phoenix Court.

sentences.zh: 其年又改城門郎為門局郎，避廟諱也。

translations.literal: That same year the Gate Attendants were renamed Gate Bureau Attendants, to avoid the taboo of the temple name.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Gate Attendants were retitled Gate Bureau Attendants to avoid the imperial temple taboo.

sentences.zh: 唐同光元年十一月，依舊為城門郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Tongguang 1 of Tang, the former title of Gate Attendant was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Tongguang 1 of Tang the former title Gate Attendant was restored.

sentences.zh: 後唐天成元年十一月，詔曰：「雄武軍節度使官銜內，宜兼押蕃落使。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Tiancheng 1 of Later Tang, an edict said: "Within the official title of the military governor of the Xiongwu Army, he should concurrently hold the post of Commissioner for Overseeing the Barbarian Tribes."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Tiancheng 1 of Later Tang an edict declared: "The military governor of the Xiongwu Army shall concurrently hold the post of Commissioner for Overseeing the Barbarian Tribes in his official title."

sentences.zh: （《職官分紀》：長興元年，分飛龍院為左右院，以小馬坊為右飛龍院。）〉

translations.literal: (Record of Official Posts by Division: In Changxing 1, the Flying Dragon Court was divided into left and right courts, with the Small Horse Pasture as the Right Flying Dragon Court.)>〉
translations.idiomatic: (Record of Official Posts by Division: In Changxing 1 the Flying Dragon Court was divided into left and right courts, with the Small Horse Pasture as the Right Flying Dragon Court.)>〉

sentences.zh: 二年七月，詔曰：「頃因本朝親王遙領方鎮，其在鎮者，遂雲副大使知節度事，但年代已深，相沿未改。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year, an edict said: "Recently because imperial princes of our court held frontier commands at a distance, those who were in the command were called deputy envoys managing military governorship affairs; but many years have passed and the usage has continued unchanged."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year two an edict declared: "Because imperial princes of our court held distant frontier commands, those stationed there were called deputy envoys managing military governorship affairs; many years have passed and the usage has continued unchanged."

sentences.zh: 今天下侯伯並正節旄，惟東、西兩川未落『副大使』字，宜令今後只言節度使。」

translations.literal: Now all lords and marquises throughout the realm hold proper command banners; only the eastern and western Two Chuan have not dropped the words 'deputy envoy.' Henceforth they should speak only of military governor."
translations.idiomatic: Now all lords and marquises throughout the realm hold proper command banners; only the eastern and western Two Chuan have not dropped the words 'deputy envoy.' Henceforth only 'military governor' shall be used."

sentences.zh: 晉天福五年四月丙午，詔曰：「承旨者，承時君之旨，非近侍重臣，無以稟朕命、宣予言。

translations.literal: On bingwu in the fourth month of Tianfu 5 of Jin, an edict said: "Expositor-in-Chief means one who carries out the timely sovereign's intent; without a close attendant and senior minister, there is no one to receive Our command and proclaim Our words.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu in the fourth month of Tianfu 5 of Jin an edict declared: "Expositor-in-Chief means one who carries out the sovereign's intent; without a close attendant and senior minister, there is no one to receive imperial command and proclaim the sovereign's words.

sentences.zh: 是以大朝會宰臣承旨，草制詔學士承旨，若無區別，何表等威。

translations.literal: Therefore at the great court assembly the chief minister is Expositor-in-Chief, and for drafting edicts the academician is Expositor-in-Chief; if there is no distinction, how can rank and authority be displayed?
translations.idiomatic: Therefore at the great court assembly the chief minister is Expositor-in-Chief, and for drafting edicts the academician is Expositor-in-Chief; without distinction, how can rank and authority be displayed?

sentences.zh: 除翰林承旨外，殿前承旨宜改為殿直，密院承旨宜改為承宣，御史臺、三司、閣門、客省所有承旨，並令別定其名。」

translations.literal: Apart from the Hanlin Expositor-in-Chief, the Expositor-in-Chief of the Palace Front should be renamed Palace Direct Attendant; the Expositor-in-Chief of the Secret Bureau should be renamed Proclaimer; all Expositors-in-Chief of the Censorate, Three Commissions, Gate of the Imperial Secretariat, and Guest Bureau should be given other names."
translations.idiomatic: Apart from the Hanlin Expositor-in-Chief, the Palace Front Expositor-in-Chief shall be renamed Palace Direct Attendant; the Secret Bureau Expositor-in-Chief shall be renamed Proclaimer; all Expositors-in-Chief of the Censorate, Three Commissions, Gate of the Imperial Secretariat, and Guest Bureau shall be given other names."

sentences.zh: 周廣順二年十二月，詔改左右威衛復為屯衛，避御名也。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of Guangshun 2 of Zhou, an edict changed the Left and Right Guards of Awesome Might back to Garrison Guards, to avoid the imperial personal name.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Guangshun 2 of Zhou an edict changed the Left and Right Guards of Awesome Might back to Garrison Guards to avoid the imperial personal name.

translations.idiomatic: —Reformed Titles—

sentences.zh: 後唐同光二年三月，中書門下奏：「糾轄之任，時謂外臺，宰字之官，古稱列爵，如非朝命，是廢國章。

translations.literal: In the third month of Tongguang 2 of Later Tang, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "The charge of oversight is called the outer platform; officials bearing the character for 'minister' were anciently called ranked nobles. If they are not by court appointment, the national regulations are abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Tongguang 2 of Later Tang the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "The charge of oversight is called the outer platform; officials bearing the character for 'minister' were anciently ranked nobles. Without court appointment the national regulations are abandoned.

sentences.zh: 近日諸道多是各列官銜，便指州縣，請朝廷之正授，樹藩鎮之私恩，頗亂規程，宜加條制。

translations.literal: Recently the circuits mostly each list official titles, then point to prefectures and districts and request proper appointment from the court, planting private favor for the frontier commands—greatly disordering the regulations; additional rules should be imposed.
translations.idiomatic: Recently circuits mostly list official titles, then point to prefectures and districts and request proper court appointment, planting private favor for frontier commands—greatly disordering regulations; additional rules should be imposed.

sentences.zh: 自今後大鎮節度使，管三州已上者，每年許奏管內官三人；

translations.literal: From now on, for military governors of great commands who govern three prefectures or more, three officials within their jurisdiction may be memorialized each year;
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth military governors of great commands governing three or more prefectures may memorialize three officials within their jurisdiction each year;

sentences.zh: 如管三州以下者，許奏管內官二人。

translations.literal: for those governing fewer than three prefectures, two officials within their jurisdiction may be memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: those governing fewer than three prefectures may memorialize two officials within their jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 仍須有課績尤異，方得上聞。

translations.idiomatic: They must have especially outstanding performance records before the matter may be reported upward.

translations.idiomatic: Defense commissioners may memorialize only one person per year; without especially outstanding merit no recommendation may be submitted.

sentences.zh: 刺史無奏薦之例，不得輒亂規程。

translations.idiomatic: Prefects have no precedent for memorializing recommendations and must not rashly disorder the regulations.

sentences.zh: 所冀招延之禮，皆合於前規；

translations.literal: It is hoped that the rites of recruitment may all accord with former rules;
translations.idiomatic: It is hoped that recruitment rites may all accord with former rules;

translations.idiomatic: investigation officers, defense and militia-training investigating officials, military judges, and the like, all after three years.

translations.idiomatic: Whenever appointment occurs, official qualification, merit rank, or office qualification should be adjusted as appropriate.

translations.idiomatic: Those with exceptionally outstanding diligence and achievement shall be considered separately for preferential advancement.

translations.idiomatic: Those whose literary learning and knowledge surpass their peers, who are praised by many, or whose worth is distinctly recognized and verified in investigation are not bound by the limit of years."

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Qingtai 2, the Secretariat and Chancellery submitted: "Formerly grand masters of the directorates, fifth-rank court officials, and western-rank generals were all allowed twenty-five full months in office; if replacement had already occurred at twenty months, they were appointed elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Qingtai 2 the Secretariat and Chancellery reported: "Formerly grand masters of the directorates, fifth-rank court officials, and western-rank generals were allowed twenty-five full months in office; if replacement occurred at twenty months they were appointed elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 少卿監，舊例三任四任方入大卿監，五品三任四任方入少卿監，今後並只三任，逐任須月限滿，無殿責者便入此官。

translations.literal: For lesser masters of the directorates, the old rule required three or four terms before entering grand master of the directorates; for fifth rank, three or four terms before entering lesser master of the directorates. Henceforth only three terms are required; each term must complete the full month quota, and those without demerit may enter these offices.
translations.idiomatic: For lesser masters of the directorates the old rule required three or four terms before grand master of the directorates; for fifth rank three or four terms before lesser master.
