sentences.zh: 西班將軍，罷任一年許求官，舊例三任四任方入大將軍，今只以三任為限，三任大將軍方入上將軍，並須逐任滿月限，無殿責，或曾任金吾將軍、街使、藩鎮刺史，特敕並不拘此例。

translations.literal: Western-rank generals, one year after leaving office, may seek appointment; the old rule required three or four terms before entering great general; now only three terms are the limit; three terms as great general before entering upper general—all must complete the full month quota in each term without demerit; or if they once served as golden guard general, street commissioner, or frontier prefect, special edicts are not bound by this rule.
translations.idiomatic: Western-rank generals may seek appointment one year after leaving office; the old rule required three or four terms before great general; now only three terms are required and three terms as great general before upper general—all must complete the full month quota without demerit; those who served as golden guard general, street commissioner, or frontier prefect are not bound by this rule under special edict.

sentences.zh: 諸道除兩使判官外，書記已下任自辟請。

translations.literal: In the circuits, apart from judges of the two commissioners, secretaries and below may be appointed by local recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the circuits, apart from judges of the two commissioners, secretaries and below may be appointed by local recommendation.

sentences.zh: 應朝官除外任，罷任後一年方許陳乞。

translations.literal: Court officials taking outside appointments may petition only one year after leaving office.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials taking outside appointments may petition only one year after leaving office.

sentences.zh: 諸道賓席未曾升朝者，若官兼三院御史，即除中下縣令；

translations.literal: Guests of the circuits who have never entered court: if their office concurrently holds censor of the three bureaus, they are appointed magistrate of a middle or lower county;
translations.idiomatic: Guests of the circuits who have never entered court: if their office concurrently holds censor of the three bureaus, they are appointed magistrate of a middle or lower county;

sentences.zh: 兼大夫、中丞、秘書少監、郎中、員外郎與清資。

translations.literal: if concurrently grand master, vice censor-in-chief, vice director of the Secretariat library, director, or vice director, they receive prestigious qualification.
translations.idiomatic: if concurrently grand master, vice censor-in-chief, vice director of the Secretariat library, director, or vice director, they receive prestigious qualification.

sentences.zh: 初任升朝官，檢校官至尚書、常侍、秘書監、庶子，升朝便與少卿監。

translations.literal: For first appointment as court official, acting commissioners up to minister, regular attendant, director of the Secretariat library, or crown prince's tutor—upon entering court they receive lesser master of the directorates.
translations.idiomatic: For first appointment as court official, acting commissioners up to minister, regular attendant, director of the Secretariat library, or crown prince's tutor—upon entering court they receive lesser master of the directorates.

sentences.zh: 諸州防禦、團練判、推官，並請本州奏辟，中書不更除授。

translations.literal: Defense and militia-training judges and investigating officials of the various prefectures should all be recommended and appointed by their prefecture; the Secretariat shall not appoint them further.
translations.idiomatic: Defense and militia-training judges and investigating officials of the prefectures shall be recommended and appointed by their prefecture; the Secretariat shall not appoint them further.

sentences.zh: 應出選門官帶三院御史供奉裏行及省銜，罷任後周年，許陳乞。

translations.literal: Officials from the selection gate bearing concurrent censor of the three bureaus, attendant in service, or provincial title may petition one full year after leaving office.
translations.idiomatic: Officials from the selection gate bearing concurrent censor of the three bureaus, attendant in service, or provincial title may petition one full year after leaving office.

sentences.zh: 諸州別駕，不除令錄，仍守本官月限，得替後一年，許陳乞。

translations.literal: Vice governors of the various prefectures are not appointed magistrates or recorders; they still observe the month quota of their original office and may petition one year after replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Vice governors of the prefectures are not appointed magistrates or recorders; they still observe the month quota of their original office and may petition one year after replacement.

sentences.zh: 長史、司馬，因攝奏正，未有官者送名。

translations.literal: Chief secretaries and aides who through acting service were memorialized for regular appointment, if they have no office, submit their names.
translations.idiomatic: Chief secretaries and aides who through acting service were memorialized for regular appointment, if they hold no office, submit their names.

sentences.zh: 三年五月乙未，詔曰：「近以內外臣僚，出入叠處，稍均勞逸，免滯轉遷，應兩司判官、畿赤令，取郎中、員外、補闕、拾遣、三丞、五博，少列宮僚，選擇擢任。

translations.literal: On yiwei in the fifth month of the third year, an edict said: "Recently, because inner and outer officials come and go in overlapping posts, to balance labor and rest somewhat and avoid stagnant promotion and transfer, for judges of the two commissioners and magistrates of the capital and red-walled prefectures, directors, vice directors, remonstrance and memorial-drafting officials, the three assistant directors, and the five erudites, and junior palace officials should be selected and promoted."
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei in the fifth month of year three an edict declared: "Because inner and outer officials rotate through overlapping posts, to balance labor and rest and avoid stagnant promotion, judges of the two commissioners and magistrates of the capital and red-walled prefectures shall be drawn from directors, vice directors, remonstrance and memorial-drafting officials, the three assistant directors, five erudites, and junior palace officials, selected and promoted."

sentences.zh: 一則俾藩方侯伯，別耀賓階；

translations.literal: First, so that frontier lords and marquises may display a distinct guest rank;
translations.idiomatic: First, so that frontier lords and marquises may display a distinct guest rank;

sentences.zh: 周廣順元年夏五月辛巳，詔：「朝廷設爵命官，求賢取士，或以資敘進，或以科級升。

translations.literal: On xinsi in the fifth summer month, Guangshun 1 of Zhou, an edict said: "The court sets ranks and orders offices, seeking the worthy and taking scholars—some advance through qualification seniority, some rise through examination grades.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi in the fifth summer month of Guangshun 1 of Zhou, an edict declared: "The court establishes ranks and appoints officials, seeking talent and selecting scholars—some advance by seniority in qualification, others rise through the examination ladder.

sentences.zh: 至有白首窮經，方諧一第；

translations.literal: Some reach white-haired age exhausting the classics before attaining one examination degree;
translations.idiomatic: Some spent their lives to white hair mastering the classics before passing a single civil examination;

sentences.zh: 半生守選，始遂一官。

translations.literal: Half a lifetime waiting on the selection rolls before at last obtaining one office.
translations.idiomatic: Others waited half a lifetime on the roster before securing a single post.

sentences.zh: 是以國無幸民，士不濫進。

translations.literal: Thus the state had no fortunate people, and scholars did not advance indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the realm had no lucky freeloaders and scholars did not flood into office without merit.

sentences.zh: 近年州郡奏薦，多無出身、前官，或因權勢書題，或是衷私請托，既難阻意，便授真恩。

translations.literal: In recent years when prefectures and districts memorialized recommendations, most had no examination degree or prior office; some relied on powerful patrons' written introductions, others on private entreaties—hard to obstruct their wishes, so genuine favors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years prefectural recommendations often came from men without degrees or prior office—some backed by powerful patrons, others by private favor—and resistance proved futile, so full appointments were granted.

sentences.zh: 遂使躁求僥幸之徒，爭遊捷徑；

translations.literal: Thus those restlessly seeking lucky chances competed to travel the quick path;
translations.idiomatic: The result was that the ambitious and opportunistic scrambled for shortcuts to office;

sentences.zh: 辛苦孤寒之士，盡泣窮途。

translations.literal: while toiling, isolated, poor scholars all wept on the road to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: while diligent scholars of humble means wept in despair at dead ends.

sentences.zh: 將期激濁揚清，所宜循名責實。

translations.literal: It is intended to stir the muddy and raise the clear; one should follow the name and demand the reality.
translations.idiomatic: To stir the muddy and raise the clear, offices must match their names and merit must match the post.

sentences.zh: 今後州府不得奏薦無前官及無出身人，如有奇才異行，越眾超群，亦許具名以聞，便可隨表赴闕，當令有司考試，朕亦親自披詳，斷其否臧，俾之升黜，庶使人不謬舉，野無遺才。」

translations.literal: Henceforth prefectures and districts shall not memorialize recommending men without prior office or without examination degree; if there are exceptional talents and conduct surpassing the multitude, they may also be reported by name; such persons may then proceed to court with the memorial; the relevant offices shall examine them; I too shall personally review and judge approval or rejection, promotion or demotion, so that people do not wrongly recommend and no talent in the wild is lost."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth no prefecture or district may recommend men without prior office or without an examination degree. Men of exceptional talent and conduct who surpass the crowd may still be reported by name and may proceed to court with the memorial; the relevant offices shall examine them, and I shall personally review each case and decide promotion or demotion, so that no one is wrongly recommended and no worthy man in obscurity is overlooked."

sentences.zh: 顯德二年六月，詔：「兩京諸道州府留守判官、兩使判官、少尹、防禦團練軍事判官，今後並不得奏薦；

translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Xiande 2 an edict declared: "Administrative assistants to resident commissioners of the two capitals and all circuits, assistants to the two commissioners, vice governors, and military administrative assistants of defense and militia-training commands may no longer be recommended by memorial;

sentences.zh: 其防禦團練、刺史州各置推官一員。

translations.literal: Right: reforms and abolitions
translations.idiomatic: —Reforms and Abolitions—

sentences.zh: 晉天福三年十一月，起居郎殷鵬上言：竊聞司封格式，內外文武臣僚才升朝籍者，無父母便與追封贈，父母在即未敘未封。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Tianfu 3 of Jin, Attendant of the Imperial Diary Yin Peng submitted: "I have heard that in the regulations of the Bureau of Enfeoffment, when civil and military officials within and without the court have just entered the court registers, if they have no parents they are at once given posthumous enfeoffment and gifts, while if parents are alive they receive no promotion of rank and no enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Tianfu 3 of Jin, Attendant of the Imperial Diary Yin Peng memorialized: "I understand that under the Bureau of Enfeoffment regulations, when civil and military officials newly enter the court registers, those without living parents receive posthumous enfeoffment at once, while those whose parents still live receive no rank promotion and no enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 以臣所見，誠為不可，此則輕生者而重死者，棄今人而錄故人，其榮有何？

translations.literal: In my view this truly cannot be allowed: this values the dead and slight the living, abandons the present person and records the old person—what honor is there in it?
translations.idiomatic: In my view this is plainly wrong: it honors the dead and slight the living, abandons the living for the sake of the dead—what glory is there in that?

sentences.zh: 其理安在？

translations.literal: Where is the principle in it?
translations.idiomatic: What principle can justify it?

sentences.zh: 又云，父母在，品秩及格者，即以封其母，不加其父，便加邑號，兼曰太君。

translations.literal: It also says that when parents are alive and rank reaches the standard, the mother alone is enfeoffed, the father is not added, yet a fief title is added and she is styled Grand Lady.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations also provide that when parents are alive and the official's rank meets the standard, only the mother is enfeoffed—the father receives nothing—yet a fief title is added and she is styled Grand Lady.

sentences.zh: 遂令妻則旁若無夫，子則上若無父，豈有父則賤而母則貴，夫則卑而妻則尊？

translations.literal: This makes the wife as if she had no husband at her side, the son as if he had no father above him—can there be a father who is base while the mother is honored, a husband who is low while the wife is exalted?
translations.idiomatic: The wife then stands as if she had no husband, the son as if he had no father—can the father be slighted while the mother is honored, the husband demeaned while the wife is exalted?

sentences.zh: 若謂其父未合加恩，安得其母受賜；

translations.literal: If one says the father is not fit to receive favor, how can the mother receive the gift;
translations.idiomatic: If the father is deemed unworthy of favor, how can the mother receive it;

sentences.zh: 若謂以子便合貴，曷得其父不先封？

translations.literal: if one says that because of the son he should be honored, how can the father not be enfeoffed first?
translations.idiomatic: if the son's rank entitles the family to honor, why is the father not enfeoffed first?

sentences.zh: 伏以父尊母卑，天地之道，尊無二上，國家同體。

translations.literal: I submit that the father is honored and the mother is base—this is the way of Heaven and Earth; honor admits no second above, and the state is of one body.
translations.idiomatic: The father is honored and the mother subordinate—such is the way of Heaven and Earth; there is no second above in honor, and the state follows the same principle.

sentences.zh: 今授封父無爵，名教不順，莫大於茲。

translations.literal: Now to grant enfeoffment to the father without a noble rank is contrary to name and teaching—nothing is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: To enfeoff the father without granting him a noble rank violates the moral order—nothing could be more serious.

sentences.zh: 臣伏乞自今後文武臣僚，父母在，其父母已有官爵者，即敘進資品以及格式，或不任祿仕，即可授以致仕或同正官，所貴得以敘封妻室。

translations.literal: I humbly beg that henceforth for civil and military officials whose parents are alive, if the parents already hold office and rank, they be promoted in qualification and rank according to the regulations, or if they cannot hold salaried office, they be granted retired status or the same regular rank as appropriate, so that enfeoffment of the wife may also be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly request that henceforth, when civil and military officials have living parents who already hold office and rank, those parents be advanced in qualification and rank under the regulations; if they cannot hold salaried office, grant them retired status or an equivalent regular rank, so that the wife may also receive enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 即父母俱榮，孝子無不逮之感；

translations.literal: Then both parents share glory, and the filial son has no feeling of failing to reach them;
translations.idiomatic: Both parents would then share in the honor, and the filial son would feel no regret at leaving them behind;

sentences.zh: 閨門交映，聖君覃慶賞之恩。

translations.literal: the inner quarters would shine together, and the sage ruler would extend the grace of reward.
translations.idiomatic: the household would shine with shared glory, and the sage ruler would extend his grace of reward.

sentences.zh: 噫！

translations.literal: Ah!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 荷陛下孝沼之風，受陛下榮親之祿者，靜而屈指，不過數人。

translations.literal: Those who receive Your Majesty's tide of filial virtue and receive Your Majesty's salary for honoring kin—counting them in stillness, they are no more than a few persons.
translations.idiomatic: Those who enjoy Your Majesty's tide of filial virtue and receive the salary of honoring kin—count them quietly, and they number only a handful.

sentences.zh: 陛下得以特議舉行，編為令式，勸天下之為善，令域中之望風，自然見前代之闕文，成我朝之盛典。

translations.literal: Your Majesty may specially deliberate and put this into practice, compile it as statute and regulation, encourage goodness throughout the realm, and let the domain look to the wind of reform—naturally the gaps of former ages will appear, and our court's great ceremony will be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty may specially deliberate and enact this, codify it as statute, encourage goodness throughout the realm, and let the realm take its cue from your example—thus the omissions of former ages will be made good and our dynasty's great ceremony will be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 況唐長興元年德音內一節『應在朝中外臣僚，父母在，並與加恩』。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the compassionate edict of Changxing 1 of Tang there is one section: 'All civil and military officials at court and without whose parents are alive shall all receive added favor.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the compassionate edict of Changxing 1 of Tang contains a passage: 'All civil and military officials at court and in the provinces whose parents are alive shall receive added favor.'

sentences.zh: 司封不行明制，堅執前文；

translations.literal: The Bureau of Enfeoffment did not carry out the clear regulation but clung to the former text;
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Enfeoffment failed to implement the clear regulation and clung to the older text;

sentences.zh: 儻布新恩，兼合舊敕，庶使事君事父，恒遵一體之規；

translations.literal: if the new favor is promulgated together with the old edict, then serving the ruler and serving the father would constantly follow one unified rule;
translations.idiomatic: if the new favor is issued together with the old edict, service to ruler and service to father would follow one unified rule;

sentences.zh: 為子為臣，不失兩全之義。

translations.literal: as son and as minister one would not lose the meaning of fulfilling both.
translations.idiomatic: as son and as minister one would not fail in either duty.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞司封令式，內外臣僚官階及五品已上者，即與封妻蔭子，固不分於清濁，但只言其品秩。

translations.literal: I also hear that in the regulations of the Bureau of Enfeoffment, for civil and military officials whose official rank reaches the fifth grade and above, wives and children are enfeoffed, without distinction of pure or impure rank—only the grade is spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: I also understand that under Bureau of Enfeoffment regulations, civil and military officials of the fifth grade and above receive enfeoffment for wife and children without regard to whether the post is prestigious or humble—only the grade matters.

sentences.zh: 且諫議大夫、給事中、中書舍人並是五品，贊善大夫、洗馬、中允、奉御等亦是五品。

translations.literal: Yet Remonstrating and Reviewing Grandee, Drafting Attendant, and Secretariat Drafter are all fifth grade; Senior Tutor, Groom, Palace Attendant, and Palace Attendant of the Imperial Household are also fifth grade.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Remonstrating and Reviewing Grandee, Drafting Attendant, and Secretariat Drafter are all fifth grade; so are Senior Tutor, Groom, Palace Attendant, and Palace Attendant of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 若論朝廷之委任，宰臣之擬論，出入之階資，中外之瞻望，則天壤相懸矣。

translations.literal: If one speaks of the court's commission, the chief ministers' nomination, the grades of entry and exit, and the gaze of within and without, then heaven and earth are separated.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the court's trust, the chief ministers' nominations, the grades of entry and exit, and the regard of court and provinces alike, the difference is as heaven from earth.

sentences.zh: 及其敘封，乃為一貫，相沿至此，甚非。

translations.literal: Yet when enfeoffment is ordered, it is all one rule—carried down to this day, this is very wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when enfeoffment is granted, all are treated alike—carried down to today, this is deeply wrong.

sentences.zh: 而況北省為陛下侍從之臣，南宮掌陛下經綸之務，憲臺執陛下紀綱之司，首冠群僚，總為三署，當職尤重，責望非輕。

translations.literal: Moreover, the northern department is Your Majesty's attendant corps, the southern palace handles Your Majesty's statecraft, the Censorate executes Your Majesty's discipline—the head of all officials, together the three offices; their duties are especially weighty, their responsibility and expectation not light.
translations.idiomatic: The northern department serves as Your Majesty's attendants, the southern palace manages statecraft, the Censorate upholds discipline—they head all officials as the three offices; their duties are especially weighty and their responsibilities not light.

sentences.zh: 此則清列十年，不遂顯榮之願；

translations.literal: Thus the pure ranks may serve ten years without fulfilling the wish for manifest glory;
translations.idiomatic: Men of the pure ranks may serve ten years without realizing their hope of distinguished honor;

sentences.zh: 彼則雜班兩任，便承封蔭之恩。

translations.literal: those of the mixed ranks, after two terms, at once receive the favor of enfeoffment and privilege.
translations.idiomatic: men of the mixed ranks, after two terms, at once receive enfeoffment and hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 事不均平，理宜改革。

translations.literal: The matter is not even and fair; reform is proper in principle.
translations.idiomatic: The imbalance is plain; reform is clearly warranted.

sentences.zh: 伏乞自今後應諸官及五品已上者，即依舊制施行，應三署清望官及六品已上，便與封蔭。

translations.literal: I humbly beg that henceforth for all officials of the fifth grade and above the old system be applied, while for prestigious officials of the three offices and the sixth grade and above, enfeoffment and privilege be granted.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly request that henceforth officials of the fifth grade and above follow the old system, while prestigious officials of the three offices and those of the sixth grade and above receive enfeoffment and hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 清濁既異，品秩宜升，仍下所司，議為恒式。

translations.literal: Since pure and impure differ, grades should be raised; still order the relevant offices to deliberate and establish a permanent rule.
translations.idiomatic: Since prestigious and humble posts differ, their grades should be distinguished; order the relevant offices to deliberate and establish a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐元年七月，詔：「尚書省集議，內外臣僚，父在，母承子蔭，敘封追封，合加『太』字否？

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Qianyou 1 of Han, an edict said: "The Department of State Affairs shall assemble for deliberation: for civil and military officials within and without, when the father is alive and the mother receives the son's privilege, in enfeoffment and posthumous enfeoffment, should the character 'Grand' be added or not? Report back.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Qianyou 1 of Han an edict ordered: "The Department of State Affairs shall deliberate whether, for civil and military officials when the father is alive and the mother receives the son's privilege, the character 'Grand' should be added in enfeoffment and posthumous enfeoffment. Report your findings.

sentences.zh: 以聞。

translations.literal: and report."
translations.idiomatic: Report back."

sentences.zh: 」尚書省奏議曰：「今詳前後敕條，凡母皆加『太』字，存歿並同。

translations.literal: The Department of State Affairs memorialized: "We have now examined the edicts and regulations before and after: for all mothers the character 'Grand' is added, whether living or dead alike.
translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs replied: "Having examined the edicts and regulations, we find that for all mothers the character 'Grand' is added, whether living or dead.

sentences.zh: 此即是父歿母存，即敘封進封內加『太』字，母歿追封，亦加『太』字，故云存歿並同。

translations.literal: This means that when the father is dead and the mother alive, in enfeoffment and promotion of enfeoffment the character 'Grand' is added; when the mother is dead and enfeoffment is posthumous, 'Grand' is also added—hence it says living and dead alike.
translations.idiomatic: This applies when the father is dead and the mother alive—in enfeoffment and promotion 'Grand' is added; when the mother is dead and enfeoffment is posthumous, 'Grand' is also added—hence 'living and dead alike.'

sentences.zh: 若是父在，據敕格無載為母加『太』字處。

translations.literal: If the father is alive, according to the edict regulations there is no provision for adding 'Grand' to the mother.
translations.idiomatic: When the father is alive, the edict regulations contain no provision for adding 'Grand' to the mother.

sentences.zh: 若以近敕，因子貴與父命官，父自有官，即妻從夫品，可以封妻，父在不合以其子加母『太』字。

translations.literal: If one follows the recent edict, because the son is honored the father is given an office; if the father already has office, the wife follows the husband's rank and the wife may be enfeoffed—the father being alive, it is not fitting to add 'Grand' to the mother through the son.
translations.idiomatic: Under the recent edict, when the son's rank entitles the father to an office and the father already holds office, the wife follows the husband's rank and may be enfeoffed—while the father lives, the son's rank should not add 'Grand' to the mother.

sentences.zh: 若雖有因子之官，其品尚卑，未得蔭妻，亦不合用子蔭之限。

translations.literal: Even if there is office through the son and the rank is still low and the wife cannot yet receive privilege, it is also not fitting to use the son's privilege limit.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the son's rank grants an office but the rank is still too low for the wife to receive privilege, the son's privilege limit should not apply.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 周顯德六年冬十二月壬辰，尚書兵部上言：「本司蔭補千牛、進馬。

translations.literal: On renchen in the twelfth winter month of Xiande 6 of Zhou, the Bureau of Military Affairs in the Department of State Affairs submitted: "This bureau supplements by privilege the Thousand-Ox and Advance Horse posts.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen in the twelfth winter month of Xiande 6 of Zhou, the Bureau of Military Affairs reported: "This bureau fills Thousand-Ox and Advance Horse posts by hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 在漢乾祐中散失敕文，自來只準《晉編敕》及堂帖施行。

translations.literal: During Han Qianyou the edict texts were scattered and lost; from that time only the Jin Compiled Edicts and bureau notices have been followed.
translations.idiomatic: During Han Qianyou the edict texts were lost; since then only the Jin Compiled Edicts and bureau notices have been followed.

sentences.zh: 伏緣前後不同，請別降敕命。

translations.literal: Because the former and latter differ, we request a separate edict.
translations.idiomatic: Because earlier and later rules differ, we request a new edict.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「今後應蔭補子孫，宜令逐品許補一人，直候轉品，方得更補，不得於本品內重疊收補。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Henceforth for descendants supplemented by privilege, each grade shall be allowed one supplement; only when the grade is transferred may another supplement be made—no overlapping supplements within the same grade.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Henceforth for descendants appointed by hereditary privilege, each grade may fill one post; only after promotion to a new grade may another appointment be made—no duplicate appointments within the same grade.

sentences.zh: 如是所補人有身故、除名、落藩、廢疾及應舉及第內，只許於本品內再補一人。

translations.literal: If the supplemented person dies, is struck from the rolls, falls from the register, is disabled, or passes the examinations and receives a degree, only one more person within the same grade may be supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: If the appointee dies, is struck from the rolls, falls from the register, is disabled, or passes the examinations and receives a degree, only one replacement within the same grade may be appointed.

sentences.zh: 太子進馬、太子千牛，不用收補。

translations.literal: Crown Prince's Advance Horse and Crown Prince's Thousand-Ox may not receive replacement supplements.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince's Advance Horse and Crown Prince's Thousand-Ox posts may not receive replacement appointments.

sentences.zh: 詹事依祭酒例施行。

translations.literal: The Household Administration of the Heir Apparent shall follow the precedent of the Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: The Household Administration of the Heir Apparent shall follow the Libationer's precedent.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書、侍郎，舊例不許收補，宜許收補。

translations.literal: Minister and Vice Minister of Military Affairs, by old precedent not allowed replacement supplements, should be allowed replacement supplements.
translations.idiomatic: Minister and Vice Minister of Military Affairs, formerly barred from replacement appointments, shall now be allowed them.

sentences.zh: 致仕官歷任中曾任在朝文班三品、武班二品及丞郎給舍已上，金吾大將軍、節度、防禦、團練、留後者，方得補蔭。

translations.literal: Retired officials who in their service once held civil rank of the third grade at court, military rank of the second grade, or Chancellor, Director, Drafting Attendant and above, or Commandant of the Golden Guard, military governor, defense commissioner, militia-training commissioner, or acting commissioner may supplement by privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Retired officials who once held third-grade civil posts at court, second-grade military posts, or posts from Chancellor and Director through Drafting Attendant and above, or Commandant of the Golden Guard, military governor, defense commissioner, militia-training commissioner, or acting commissioner may appoint by privilege.

sentences.zh: 皇蔭人，其祖、父曾授著皇朝官秩，方得收補。

translations.literal: For imperial privilege appointees, only when grandfather and father once received official rank in the present dynasty may replacement supplements be received.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial privilege appointees may receive replacements only when grandfather and father once held official rank in the present dynasty.

sentences.zh: 應合收補人，須是本官親子孫年貌合格，別無渝濫，方許施行。

translations.literal: Persons fit for replacement supplement must be the official's own children or grandchildren of qualified age and appearance, with no irregularity, before implementation is permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Replacement appointees must be the official's own children or grandchildren of qualified age and appearance, with no irregularity, before appointment is permitted.

sentences.zh: 余從舊例處分。」

translations.literal: The remainder shall be handled according to old precedent."
translations.idiomatic: All other matters shall follow established precedent."

sentences.zh: 右封蔭

translations.literal: Right: hereditary privilege
translations.idiomatic: —Hereditary Privilege—

sentences.zh: 梁開平四年四月，敕：「諸州鎮使，官秩無高卑，並在縣令之下。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Kaiping 4 of Liang, an edict said: "All circuit commissioners, regardless of rank high or low, are all below the county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Kaiping 4 of Liang an edict declared: "All circuit commissioners, regardless of rank, rank below the county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 」其年九月，詔曰：「魏博管內刺史，比來州務，並委督郵，遂使曹官擅其威權，州牧同於閑冗，俾循通制，宜塞異端，並宜依河南諸州例，刺史得以專達。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year, an edict said: "Prefects within the Weibo circuit—in recent years circuit affairs have all been entrusted to supervising clerks, so that bureau officials usurped their authority and the prefect was like one idle and redundant; to follow the universal regulation and stop irregular practices, all should follow the example of the Henan prefectures: the prefect may report directly.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of that year an edict declared: "Prefects in the Weibo circuit have long had their duties delegated to supervising clerks, leaving bureau officials with the power and prefects idle; to restore proper practice and stop abuses, all shall follow the Henan prefectures: prefects may report directly to court.

sentences.zh: 」時議者曰：「唐朝憲宗時，烏重胤為滄州節度使，嘗以河朔十六州能抗拒朝命者，以奪刺史權與縣令職而自作威福耳。

translations.literal: Commentators of the time said: "In the time of Emperor Xianzong of Tang, Wu Chongyin was military governor of Cangzhou and once said that the sixteen prefectures of the Yellow River north could resist court commands because they stripped the prefects of authority and gave county magistrate duties to themselves to make their own power and blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries remarked: "Under Emperor Xianzong of Tang, Wu Chongyin, military governor of Cangzhou, observed that the sixteen Yellow River north prefectures could defy the court because they stripped prefects of authority and kept county magistrates under their own control to monopolize power.

sentences.zh: 若二千石各得其柄，又有鎮兵，雖安、史挾奸，豈能據一墉而叛哉！

translations.literal: If each two-thousand-bushel official obtained his handle and there were also garrison troops, even if An and Shi held treachery, how could they have seized one walled city and rebelled!
translations.idiomatic: Had each prefect held his proper authority and garrison troops answered to him, even An Lushan and Shi Siming could not have seized a single walled city and rebelled!

sentences.zh: 遂奏以所管德、棣、景三州，各還刺史職分，州兵並隸收管。

translations.literal: He then memorialized that in the three prefectures of De, Di, and Jing under his jurisdiction, each should restore the prefect's proper duties, and prefectural troops should all be placed under his receipt and control.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that in De, Di, and Jing—the three prefectures under his command—each prefect's proper authority should be restored and prefectural troops placed under his control.

sentences.zh: 是後雖幽、鎮、魏三道，以河北舊風，自相傳襲，惟滄州一道，獨稟命受代，自重胤制置使然也。

translations.literal: Thereafter, though You, Zhen, and Wei three circuits by the old customs of Hebei transmitted and inherited among themselves, only the Cangzhou circuit alone received orders and accepted replacement—this was due to Chongyin's arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, though You, Zhen, and Wei circuits continued the old Hebei custom of hereditary succession, only Cangzhou accepted imperial orders and regular replacement—owing to Chongyin's reforms.

sentences.zh: 則梁氏之更張，正合其事矣。」

translations.literal: Then the Liang dynasty's changes fit the matter exactly."
translations.idiomatic: The Liang dynasty's reforms thus addressed precisely this problem."

sentences.zh: 後唐長興二年閏五月，詔曰：「要道才行，則千岐共貫；

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month of Changxing 2 of Later Tang, an edict said: "Where the vital path requires ability, a thousand branches share one thread;
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of Changxing 2 of Later Tang an edict declared: "Where the vital path requires talent, a thousand branches follow one thread;

sentences.zh: 宏綱一舉，則萬目畢張。

translations.literal: when the great net is raised, ten thousand eyes are all opened.
translations.idiomatic: when the great framework is raised, ten thousand eyes open at once.

sentences.zh: 前王之法制罔殊，百代之科條悉在，無煩改作，各有定規，守程式者心逸日休，率胸臆者心勞日拙。

translations.literal: The laws and institutions of former kings are not different; the statutes of a hundred generations are all preserved—there is no need for troublesome reform, each having its fixed rule; those who keep the forms and procedures find their hearts at ease and days at rest, while those who follow their own breasts find their hearts weary and days clumsy.
translations.idiomatic: Former kings' laws differ little; statutes of a hundred generations remain on record—no needless reform is required, for each has its fixed rule. Those who keep to procedure find their hearts at ease; those who follow private impulse find their hearts weary and their days unproductive.

sentences.zh: 天垂萬象，星辰之分野靡差；

translations.literal: Heaven hangs ten thousand images, and the divisions of the stars are not in error;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven displays ten thousand images, and the stars keep their divisions without error;

sentences.zh: 地載群倫，嶽瀆之方隅不易。

translations.literal: earth bears all classes, and the directions of mountains and rivers do not change.
translations.idiomatic: earth bears all peoples, and the directions of mountains and rivers do not shift.

sentences.zh: 儻各司其局，則皆盡其心。

translations.literal: If each office keeps its post, then all will exhaust their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: If each office keeps to its charge, all will give their full effort.

sentences.zh: 且律令、格式、六典，凡關庶政，互有區分，久不舉行，遂至隳紊。

translations.literal: Moreover, statutes, regulations, formats, and the Six Institutions—everything touching common administration has mutual distinctions; long unenforced, they have come to ruin and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes, regulations, formats, and the Six Institutions—all matters of common administration have their distinctions; long neglected, they have fallen into disorder.

sentences.zh: 宜準舊制，令百司各於其間錄出本局公事，巨細一一抄寫，不得漏落纖毫，集成卷軸，仍粉壁書在公廳。

translations.literal: It is fitting to follow the old system and order each of the hundred offices to extract from among them the public business of its bureau, great and small copied one by one, with not the slightest omission, assembled into scrolls, and still written on whitewashed walls in the public hall.
translations.idiomatic: Follow the old system: order each office to extract its public business from these sources, copying every item great and small without omission, assemble the copies into scrolls, and post them on whitewashed walls in the public hall.

sentences.zh: 若未有廨署者，文書委官司主掌，仍每有新授官到，令自寫錄一本披尋。

translations.literal: Where there is not yet a bureau office, documents shall be entrusted to the bureau in charge; moreover, whenever a newly appointed official arrives, he shall copy one volume himself for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Where no bureau office yet exists, the supervising bureau shall hold the documents; whenever a newly appointed official arrives, he shall copy one volume for his own reference.

sentences.zh: 或因顧問之時，應對須知次弟，無容曠闕。

translations.literal: Or when there is consultation, in answering one must know the order—there must be no neglect or gap.
translations.idiomatic: When consulted, he must know the proper sequence of business and leave no gap in his answers.

sentences.zh: 每在執行，使庶僚則守法奉公，宰臣則提綱振領，必當彜倫攸敘。

translations.literal: Whenever it is carried out, let the multitude of officials keep the law and serve with integrity, and let the chief ministers raise the net and shake the collar—then the constant relations will surely be ordered.
translations.idiomatic: In daily execution, let subordinates keep the law and serve faithfully, and let chief ministers hold the reins and set the tone—then the moral order will be preserved.

sentences.zh: 所謂至道不繁，何必期年，然後報政。

translations.literal: What is called the utmost Way is not elaborate—why must one wait a full year before reporting on government?
translations.idiomatic: The highest Way is not elaborate—why wait a full year before governance shows results?

sentences.zh: 宜令御史臺遍加告諭催促，限兩月內鈔錄及粉壁書寫須畢，其間或有未可便行，及曾厘革事件，委逐司旋申中書門下，當更參酌，奏覆施行。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order the Censorate to proclaim and urge throughout; within two months copying and whitewashed-wall writing must be completed; if among them there are matters not yet fit for immediate enforcement, or events of former reform and abolition, each bureau shall promptly report to the Secretariat and Chancellery, which shall further deliberate and memorialize for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Order the Censorate to proclaim and urge compliance; copying and wall posting must be completed within two months. Matters not fit for immediate enforcement, or former reforms and abolitions, each bureau shall report promptly to the Secretariat and Chancellery for further deliberation and memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 」其年八月，敕：「今後大理寺官員，宜同臺省官例升進，其法直官，比禮直官任使。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year, an edict said: "Henceforth officials of the Court of Judicial Review shall advance like officials of the Censorate and Secretariat; the law officers shall be employed like the ritual officers."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of that year an edict declared: "Henceforth Court of Judicial Review officials shall advance by the same rules as Censorate and Secretariat officials; law officers shall be employed on the same terms as ritual officers."

sentences.zh: 應順元年春三月戊午，宗正上言：「故事，諸陵有令、丞各一員，近令、丞不俱置，便委本縣令兼之。

translations.literal: On wuwu in the third month of spring, Yingshun 1, the Court of the Imperial Clan submitted: "By precedent, each imperial tomb had one Director and one Assistant; recently Directors and Assistants have not both been established, and the local county magistrate was entrusted to hold the post concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu in the third spring month of Yingshun 1, the Court of the Imperial Clan reported: "By precedent each imperial tomb had one Director and one Assistant; recently both posts have not been filled, and the local county magistrate has held the duties concurrently.

sentences.zh: 緣河南、洛陽是京邑，恐兼令、丞不便。

translations.literal: Because Henan and Luoyang are the capital districts, we fear concurrent magistrate and tomb posts are inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Because Henan and Luoyang are the capital districts, we fear concurrent service as magistrate and tomb officer is impractical.

sentences.zh: 」詔特置陵臺令、丞各一員。

translations.literal: An edict specially established one Tomb Platform Director and one Assistant each.
translations.idiomatic: An edict specially established one Tomb Platform Director and one Assistant for each tomb.

sentences.zh: 右雜錄

translations.literal: Right: miscellaneous records
translations.idiomatic: —Miscellaneous Records—
